title: AlphaGeo Global Climate Risk Indicators
meta_info: Asset Valuation,Real Estate & Property Management,ESG Investment Analysis,Regulatory Reporting,Risk Analysis
description:
Translate climate models and macro trends into the physical impact of climate risk on any location globally. Climate volatility is redefining both geography and the investment landscape​. A 2-degree warmer world will increasingly be divided between zones suitable and unsuitable for habitation. Humans must adapt accordingly, primarily through significant new infrastructure investment and migration.​

What We Do: 

Climate Alpha is the first in the market to offer three CMIP6* scenarios across six major risk categories. We also predict multiple climate change scenarios when data is only available for one. For example, storm surge forecasts are only available for SSP585, but we engineer the data for SSP240 and SSP370 as well. This is achieved by employing proprietary ML approaches that downscale climate models using H3 geospatial indexing technology to provide simulations at the most granular coordinate level. These methods also ensure our ability to seamlessly integrate the next iteration of global climate models such as the Earth System Model (ESM). 

The Product: 

Global Climate Risk Indicators assist users in gauging the physical impact of climate risk on any location globally — by country, state/province and city. Each of the (6) indicators (Heat Stress, Wildfire, Coast Flooding, Inland Flooding, Hurricane Wind, Drought) are made up of features, i.e., ~50 underlying datasets that inform the value of each individual physical risk score.

Each feature is available in 4 different periods (2025, 2035, 2050, 2100) and 3 climate emission pathways (SSP245, SSP370. SSP585)

Our Data:

We collect and harness a growing database of raw, unstructured​ data sources across a wide range of categories and have created in-house feature engineering pipelines to extract explainable features from them. These unstructured datasets —  such as GIS mobility, remote sensing images, and location-based text data —  contain rich, alternative information such as market and political sentiments, migration, capital flows, regulatory signals and other value-impacting indicators. We have built custom data mining pipelines to extract these data using computer vision and NLP algorithms. 
________________________________________________________________________________________

*Climate change scenarios are based on the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project 6 (CMIP6), which project greenhouse gas emissions under different climate policies until the year 2100.

title: England (Major) Roads Traffic Data
description:
National Traffic Information Service traffic data for major roads in England (across 000s of network links) National Traffic Information Service (NTIS) collects traffic data from various sensors and makes them available in isolation or as “fused” services. The processed data is averaged across all lanes of the carriageway and reported on a per network link basis every minute. This is known as the Processed Traffic Data (PTD). Sensor-only data is that which has been collected from sensors on the road including data from MIDAS Gold sites every minute and from TMU and ANPR equipment every 5 minutes. Data such as speed, flows, occupancy, headway and travel times is processed and reported on a per network link basis.

Full details of the raw NTIS Datex II service can be found at this URL
https://www.trafficengland.com/resources/cms-docs/user-guide.pdf

Tables include:
- Traffic Metrics by Event (Traffic Flow, Traffic Concentration, Traffic Headway, Traffic Speed, Travel Time Data for each PTD Network Link/Event)

Fields include:
- Network Link ID
- Datetime of Event/Measurement
- Measurement Type (d2lm:TrafficFlow, d2lm:TrafficConcentration, d2lm:TrafficHeadway, d2lm:TrafficSpeed, d2lm:TravelTimeData)
- Measurement Value

title: ANNUAL CONSUMPTION OF ELECTRICITY AND GAS BY DEPARTMENT AND BY SECTOR OF ACTIVITY
meta_info: Energy Planning,Market Research,Infrastructure Development,Environmental Assessment,Investment Decisions,Benchmarking
description:
Explore 2011-2021's energy consumption trends by sector and region in France This dataset enables users to visualize the evolution of electricity and gas consumption from 2011 to 2021 by sector of activity  and by department. The data respects commercial sensitivity rules and is based on the INSEE reference as of January 1, 2021.

A methodological note is included. For further questions or for sharing use cases, the Open Data Electricity and Gas Experts Forum is available on https://www.agenceore.fr/forum-expert.

Fields Included:


Operator (Opérateur): Represents the operator or company responsible for energy production or distribution.

Year (Année): This field refers to the year in which the data was recorded.

Sector (Filière): This signifies the type of energy, such as gas or electricity.

Agricultural Consumption (Consommation Agriculture (MWh)): Represents the total amount of energy consumed in the agricultural sector.

Number of Agricultural Points (Nombre de points Agriculture): Provides the number of data points related to the agricultural sector.

Number of Secretised Grids (Agriculture) (Nombre de mailles secretisées (agriculture)): Field under this title.

Agricultural Quality Indicator (Indique qualité Agriculture): Indicates the reliability of agricultural consumption data.

Industrial Consumption (Consommation Industrie (MWh)): Represents the total amount of energy consumed in the industrial sector.

Number of Industrial Points (Nombre de points Industrie): Provides the number of data points related to the industrial sector.

Number of Secretised Grids (Industry) (Nombre de mailles secretisées (industrie)): Field under this title.

Industrial Quality Indicator (Indice qualité Industrie): Indicates the reliability of industrial consumption data.

Tertiary Consumption (Consommation Tertiaire (MWh)): Represents the total amount of energy consumed in the tertiary sector, which typically includes services and commerce.

Number of Tertiary Points (Nombre de points Tertiaire): Provides the number of data points related to the tertiary sector.

Number of Secretised Grids (Tertiary) (Nombre de mailles secretisées (tertiaire)): Field under this title.

Tertiary Quality Indicator (Indice qualité Tertiaire): Indicates the reliability of tertiary consumption data.

Residential Consumption (Consommation Résidentiel (MWh)): Represents the total amount of energy consumed in the residential sector.

Number of Residential Points (Nombre de points Résidentiel): Provides the number of data points related to the residential sector.

Number of Secretised Grids (Residential) (Nombre de mailles secretisées (résidentiel)): Field under this title.

Residential Quality Indicator (Indice qualité Résidentiel): Indicates the reliability of residential consumption data.

Unknown Sector Consumption (Consommation Secteur Inconnu (MWh)): Represents the total amount of energy consumed in unclassified or unknown sectors.

Number of Unknown Sector Points (Nombre de points Secteur Inconnu): Provides the number of data points related to the unclassified sectors.

Number of Secretised Grids (Unknown Sector) (Nombre de mailles secretisées (secteur inconnu)): Field under this title.

Non-Allocated Quality Indicator (Indice qualité Non Affecté): Indicates the reliability of data for the unclassified sectors.

Department Code (Code Département): The unique code that identifies a department (an administrative region in France).

Department Label (Libellé Département): The name of the department.

Region Code (Code Région): The unique code that identifies a region in France.

Region Label (Libellé Région): The name of the region.

Sector id (id_filiere): A unique identifier for the energy kind.

Geometry (geom): Geographical data related to the locations associated with the data.

Total Consumption (Consommation totale (MWh)): Represents the total energy consumption across all sectors.

title: ANNUAL REGIONAL PRODUCTION OF RENEWABLE ENERGIES IN FRANCE 2008 TO 2022
meta_info: Renewable Energy Investment,Policy Development,Market Entry Strategy,Infrastructure Planning,Sustainability Benchmarking, Climate Impact Assessment
description:
Trace the annual regional renewable energy production in France, considering diverse energy sources since 2008 This dataset tracks annual renewable energy production by region in France from 2008 for electricity and from 2015 for gas. The data includes specific sources such as hydro, bioenergy, wind, and solar energy, providing insights into the landscape of renewable energy production in France. It serves as a valuable tool for stakeholders interested in the development and trends of renewable energy across different regions in the country.

Fields Included:

Year (Annee): Represents the year in which the data was recorded.

Region Name (INSEE) (Nom INSEE région): Identifies the region's name as recorded by the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).

Region Code (INSEE) (Code INSEE région): Represents the unique code identifying a region in France, as per the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).

Renewable Hydroelectric Production (Production hydraulique renouvelable (GWh)): Shows the total amount of renewable energy produced through hydroelectric means in gigawatt-hours.

Renewable Bioenergy Production (Production bioénergies renouvelable (GWh)): Indicates the total amount of renewable energy produced from bioenergy sources in gigawatt-hours.

Renewable Wind Production (Production éolienne renouvelable (GWh)): Depicts the total amount of renewable energy produced from wind power in gigawatt-hours.

Renewable Solar Production (Production solaire renouvelable (GWh)): Designates the total amount of renewable energy produced from solar power in gigawatt-hours.

Renewable Electric Production (Production électrique renouvelable (GWh)): Signifies the total amount of renewable energy produced for electricity in gigawatt-hours.

Renewable Gas Production (Production gaz renouvelable (GWh)): Highlights the total amount of renewable energy produced for gas in gigawatt-hours.

Total Renewable Production (Production totale renouvelable (GWh)): Reveals the total amount of renewable energy produced in all sectors in gigawatt-hours.

Region Geo-Shape (Géo-shape région): Contains geographic data showing the shape of the region, suitable for map plotting or other geographic analysis.

Region Geo-Point (Géo-point région): Features a single geographic point representing the location of the region, usually in latitude and longitude coordinates.

Our international partners and clients, including industry leaders like Siemens, Siemens Energy, Bosch, and Bayer, rely on our data and methodologies for their annual reporting. 

Decarbonization is a major challenge that businesses face today: they must accomplish a great deal in a short period of time. The biggest share of carbon emissions arises somewhere along the supply chain, forcing companies to invest a lot of time and resources into tedious data hunts. ctrl+s provides a short cut: cutting-edge solutions to help achieve transparency of global supply chain emissions. 

Our database matter+s provides a unique set of over 150,000 consistent emission factors covering all imaginable products and services, while considering the distinct performance of all 250 countries in the world. All emission factors are updated every quarter. matter+s offers in-depth insights into the root causes rather than only providing overall impact or risk figures. 

In contrast to alternative approaches, matter+s stands out for its high efficiency and pragmatic utilization of readily available procurement data. Its hybrid approach effectively bridges the gap between spend-based and LCA-based methodologies, simplifying scope 3 accounting. With its strong alignment with standards like the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, CDP, Science Based Targets initiative, matter+s gains trust and reliability, ensuring its credibility as a solution for sustainable supply chain management. 

To accurately calculate emissions, simply integrate our dataset with your readily available spend data and multiply our precise emission factor with the spend volume of each corresponding spend item. It’s a straightforward process that ensures accurate measurement of your environmental impacts.

title: Automatic Carbon Footprinting (Scope 1, 2 & 3) - Sample
meta_info: Automated Emission Calculations,Informed Decision Making,Trustworthy Reporting
description:
Convert operational data into carbon emission metrics, automatically. Enterprises worldwide use Climatiq's carbon calculation engine to incorporate emission intelligence into their daily operations and speed up their journey toward achieving net-zero emissions.

By integrating our Open Emission Factor Database with Snowflake, Climatiq allows users to analyze, report, and forecast their business emissions accurately and automatically using emission metrics. These calculations are based on the largest, scientifically vetted database of emission factors, which includes over 50,000 factors covering 300 global territories and all major economic sectors. The data in this database is sourced from governmental bodies and meets the standards of the GHG Protocol and other industry standards.

This sample only provides 20 random emission factors without any intelligent pre-processing of your activity data. The full database access covers 20k+ factors as well as unit and currency conversion, data mapping, and distance calculation capabilities. 
___________________________

Use cases for business carbon footprinting: 
# Scope 1 emissions: 
- Company-owned vehicles, e.g. cars, vans and trucks, 
- Company-owned boilers, furnaces, and other fuel-burning equipment
- On-site generation of electricity, steam, or hot water using fossil fuels
- Use of refrigerants in air conditioning and refrigeration equipment
- Flaring of waste gasses at industrial facilities

# Scope 2 emissions:
- Electricity purchased from the grid and used by your organisation
- Steam or hot water purchased from a utility company and used by your organisation
- Use of district heating or cooling systems

# Scope 3 emissions:
- Use of products or services provided by your organisation
- Transportation of goods or materials to or from your facilities
- Business travel, such as air travel and car rentals
- Disposal or recycling of generated waste
- Use of leased or rented equipment
- Extraction, production, and processing of raw materials that are used by the organisation


Expected Workflow for the full access
1. Define which activities to measure, e.g. business travel, procured goods and services, or cloud computing.
2. Locate the relevant activity data within your data lake, e.g. the information on your energy consumption.

Option 1 
3. Climatiq shares the full Open Emission Factor Database with the user
4. The user identifies the relevant emission factors himself and uses them to calculate the emissions of the activities

Option 2
3. User shares this activity data (incl. the corresponding consumption parameters, e.g. kWh of energy consumed, and further metadata, e.g. the region and year of the consumption) with Climatiq via the data share
4. Climatiq selects the most relevant emission factor based on the activity type, region, and other metadata, converts units, currencies, or distances where appropriate, and shares the results back with the user via the data share
5. User stores the results to further use for analytics and emission insights.


Calculation results include:
- The overall emissions as CO2 equivalent (CO2e)
- Details of the calculation (chosen emission factor, metadata)  
- Breakdown by individual greenhouse gas if available (e.g. methane)
- If applicable, interim results such as the calculated distance and route for transport


Getting started:

title: Fraud Detection with Synthetic Data
meta_info: Data Quality and Cleansing,Machine Learning,Risk Analysis
description:
A synthetically generated dataset, created to represent a mortgage fraud detection use case. This dataset is a synthetic dataset designed to simulate mortgage applications in a banking context, with the aim of identifying potentially fraudulent instances. Each row in the dataset represents a unique mortgage application, including various applicant details, property information, and financial metrics. The dataset has been engineered to include a mix of legitimate and fraudulent applications, providing a comprehensive base for developing and evaluating fraud detection models. Different variations of the dataset can be generated depending on specific needs, feel free to contact us for more information.

This synthetic dataset can be utilized for various purposes, including:
- Developing machine learning models for detecting mortgage fraud in a banking context.
- Evaluating the performance of different fraud detection algorithms.
- Analyzing and understanding the patterns and characteristics of fraudulent mortgage applications.
- Training and validating models that can generalize well to real-world mortgage application data.

The synthetic dataset was generated using an agent-based method calibrated on a real-life scenario and augmented using generative models. Agents are designed to represent individuals from specific geographical areas. A small number of agents are designed to assume fraudulent behavior by providing specific patterns and rules (provided with the final documentation) that will characterize the final dataset.

Tables Included:
The dataset includes two tables: 
- Customers, a table describing the anagraphic of the applicants 
- Applications, a table describing each mortgage request

Fields Included:

Customers Table:
- Applicant ID (integer): A unique identifier for each applicant.
- Applicant Name (string): First name of the applicant.
- Applicant Last name (string): Last name of the applicant.
- Date of Birth (date): The applicant's date of birth.
- City of Birth (string): The applicant's city of birth.
- Country of Birth (string): The applicant's country of birth.
- Employment Status (string): The applicant's current employment status (e.g., Employed, Self-employed, Unemployed, Retired).
- Annual Income (float): The applicant's total annual income in USD.
- Credit Score (integer): The applicant's credit score at the time of application.
-Previous Foreclosures (integer): The number of previous foreclosures, if any, on the applicant's record.
- Bankruptcies (integer): The number of bankruptcies, if any, on the applicant's record.

Applications Table:
- Application ID (integer): A unique identifier for each mortgage application.
- Applicant ID (integer)(foreign key): A unique identifier for each mortgage application.
- Date of Application (date): The date on which the mortgage application was submitted.
- Property Address (string): The address of the property for which the mortgage is being sought.
- Property Type (string): The type of property (e.g., Single Family Home, Multi-family Home, Condominium, Townhouse).
- Property Value (float): The current market value of the property in USD.
- Loan Amount (float): The requested mortgage loan amount in USD.
- Loan Term (integer): The number of years for the mortgage loan term.
- Loan-to-Value Ratio (float): The ratio of the loan amount to the property value, expressed as a percentage.
- Debt-to-Income Ratio (float): The applicant's total monthly debt payments divided by their gross monthly income, expressed as a percentage.
- Fraud Indicator (boolean): A binary indicator of whether the mortgage application is fraudulent (1) or legitimate (0).

Sources:
- https://www.jpmorgan.com/technology/technology-blog/synthetic-data-for-real-insights
- https://www.clearbox.ai/use-cases/improving-fraud-detection
- https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sgpjesus/bank-account-fraud-dataset-neurips-2022

title: Renewable Electricity Netherlands
description:
Netherlands' Renewable Electricity Transition: A Sustainable Shift Introduction:
The Dutch Renewable Electricity Production Dataset is a comprehensive collection of information on the production of renewable electricity in the Netherlands. It offers valuable insights into the renewable energy landscape, energy source distribution, installed capacity, and electricity production trends over the years. This dataset can be utilized by researchers, policymakers, analysts, and businesses to gain a deep understanding of the renewable energy sector's growth, sustainability, and contribution to the overall electricity supply. Whether you are an environmental enthusiast, a policy-maker shaping the energy transition, or a business looking to invest in the renewable energy market, this dataset will provide you with the data necessary for informed decision-making and strategic planning.

Scope and Value:
The dataset covers the period from 1990 to the latest available year (2022) and includes both historical and the most recent data. It provides extensive information on various aspects of renewable electricity production, including energy source techniques, gross and net electricity production figures, installation statistics, and electrical capacity. Moreover, the dataset offers normalized production values to correct for weather conditions and indirect production from green gas, giving a more accurate representation of renewable electricity generation. This normalization allows for fair comparisons and trend analysis.

Field Examples:
YEAR: 1990, 1991, 1992, ..., 2020, 2021, 2022

CBS is the national statistical office of the Netherlands, responsible for collecting and publishing reliable statistical information on various aspects of Dutch society, including energy and environment. The data is collected from energy companies, regulatory bodies, and other relevant sources, ensuring its accuracy and consistency.

Conclusion:
The Dutch Renewable Electricity Production Dataset offers a wealth of valuable information that can be harnessed for diverse purposes. It serves as a critical resource for researchers, policymakers, analysts, and businesses to understand the renewable energy landscape in the Netherlands and make informed decisions. Whether you are tracking the growth of renewable energy, planning investments, or developing sustainable policies, this dataset provides the foundation for comprehensive analysis and data-driven insights. Harness the power of renewable energy data to shape a greener and more sustainable future for the Netherlands and beyond.

title: Milk Supply and Dairy Production Netherlands
description:
Dutch Dairy: Navigating Milk Supply and Sustainable Production Introduction:
Welcome to the Netherlands Milk Supply and Dairy Production Dataset! This comprehensive dataset provides valuable insights into the dairy industry in the Netherlands. It encompasses data on the volume of cows' milk delivered by dairy farmers, the production of various dairy products, and important nutritional components like fat and protein content. Whether you're a researcher, policymaker, or industry professional, this dataset offers a goldmine of information to explore and understand the dynamics of one of the key sectors in the Dutch economy.

Scope, Scale, and Value:
The dataset covers a vast scope, spanning multiple years and providing both monthly and yearly figures. The dataset's scale is impressive, with records from various dairy factories, amounting to approximately 96% of all raw cows' milk produced in the country. By analyzing this data, you can gain a comprehensive understanding of the Netherlands' dairy industry, including supply patterns, production trends, and the economic significance of dairy products.

Sample Fields:
YEAR: Year of record (e.g., 2021, 2022).
MONTH: Month of record (e.g., Jan, Feb, Mar).
VOLUME: The volume of cows' milk delivered in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 2000, 2100).
BUTTER: Amount of butter produced in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 300, 290).
FAT_CONTENT: Fat content of raw cows' milk as a percentage (e.g., 3.5, 3.7).
PROTEIN_CONTENT: Protein content in raw cows' milk as a percentage (e.g., 3.2, 3.1).
TOTAL_MILK_POWDER: Total milk powder (whole and skimmed) production in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 500, 550).
WHOLE_MILK_POWDER: Milk powder with 1.5 percent or more fat production in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 200, 180).
SKIMMED_MILK_POWDER: Milk powder with less than 1.5 percent fat production in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 150, 160).
CONCENTRATED_MILK: Thickened milk or concentrated milk production in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 50, 40).
CHEESE: Cheese made of cows' milk only production in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 400, 380).
WHEY_POWDER: Whey (in powdered or block form) production in 1000 kilograms (e.g., 50, 55).
Data Sources:
The data in this dataset is sourced from the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), which gathers data from various dairy factories across the Netherlands. The agency provides both monthly and yearly statistics for dairy products. The monthly figures are based on around 98% of all cows' milk delivered to dairy factories, with a provisional adjustment made by the agency. These monthly figures are later revised when the yearly figures become available. The dataset does not include figures about fresh dairy products for consumption or acidified milk products, such as yogurts. Additional data about these products is available for the years 1995-1997.

Conclusion:
The Netherlands Milk Supply and Dairy Production Dataset offers a comprehensive and up-to-date resource for understanding the dairy industry's dynamics in the Netherlands. Whether you're an academic researcher, a policymaker looking to make data-driven decisions, or an industry professional seeking market insights, this dataset will provide you with valuable information to unlock various opportunities and drive growth in the dairy sector. Happy exploring!

title: Macrobond Pay-As-You-Go Data
meta_info: Quantitative Analysis,Economic Impact Analysis,ESG Investment Analysis,Machine Learning,Fundamental Analysis,Risk Analysis
description:
300+ million macroeconomic and financial time series with point-in-time vintages The Macrobond data feed available on Snowflake can deliver any of the time series belonging to the Macrobond's database. 

Collected from over 2,500 national and international sources, supplemented by third-party premium databases available on Macrobond ONE: https://www.macrobond.com/solutions/macrobond-one (subject to licensing), it offers access to the broadest macroeconomic and financial time series database in the world. From developed to emerging and frontier markets, time series are delivered with full history, an extensive set of metadata, and point-in-time vintages where available. 

Time series updates are pushed into your Snowflake tables and views in real-time as well as delivered instantly when you add or remove time series from your universe, through a dedicated Macrobond data feed management portal. 

Data share workflow:

1. [Provided by Macrobond] Find the time series you need via the Macrobond data catalogue (Macrobond.net)

2. [Provided by Macrobond] Subscribe to one of the yearly data plans provided by Macrobond Pay-As-You-Go and add the time series you need to the management portal

3. [Provided in Snowflake] Consume the selected time series in your Snowflake instance from the table and views below:

  - [TABLE] MAIN_ENTITY: to retrieve all of your time series with dates, values, metadata, and vintages. Time series are provided in nested objects.
  - [VIEWS] LATEST_ENTITY: to retrieve the latest version of each time series only, derived from the latest vintage available in MAIN_ENTITY, containing dates and values, and metadata.
  - [TABLE] REVISION: to access point-in-time vintages of your time series (where applicable)
  - [VIEWS] SUBSCRIPTION: providing a summary of your subscribed universe with a few metadata fields such 'number of revisions' or 'last update in Snowflake'

Make a use of Snowflake's SQL queries to flatten the json objects and retrieve a tabular version of your time series and the associated metadata fields.

title: Raw ESG data of 10,000+ listed companies in Europe, including scope 1, 2 & 3
meta_info: ESG Investment Analysis,Economic Impact Analysis,Risk Analysis,Market Analysis,Quantitative Analysis
description:
Our dataset includes both reported and modeled emissions, spanning up to 10 years of historical ESG data. # Introduction

This carbon emissions dataset provides an overview of the scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions of publicly listed companies in Europe. Oxari ensures full data coverage across all three scopes by leveraging AI to model emission profiles of companies that partly report or lack reporting at all. Our AI based methodology incorporates various factors to precisely model emission data. These factors include for example industry specifics, balance sheet data and financial statements.

# Our approach

Unlike traditional approaches that rely solely on directly reported data and pre-existing databases, we leverage the latest developments in AI and machine learning to model corporate carbon emissions when reporting is lacking. More information about our model can be found in the linked documentation. Following this approach we provide access to reported and modeled emission data for over 10,000 companies.

# Use cases

- **Historic emissions modeling:** With our in house developed AI models we calculated historic emissions of individual companies and portfolios.
- **Dataset completion:** Our AI models enable you to fill gaps in emission datasets effortlessly. For example, if scope 3 is missing, we model the expected scope 3 value and include it in the data ensuring 100% data coverage.
- **Carbon footprint assessment:** With our data you can assess the environmental impact of any investment portfolio by quantifying carbon emissions associated with each holding.
- **Identify environmental leaders and laggards:** Oxari facilitates informed decision making, since you can identify the frontrunners and laggards in emission reduction efforts.
- **Decoupling evaluation:** You can evaluate the decoupling scale of companies by analyzing their economic growth pathway and compare it to their climate impact and emissions.

# AI pipeline

Our AI pipeline consists of five steps, starting with data collection and cleaning all the to emission modeling. The process is as follows:

1. **Data collection:** Oxari gathers granular emission data from trusted sources, such as the OECD and company reports.
2. **Data cleaning:** We validate the collected datapoints both manually and automatically to ensure data integrity.
3. **Categorize scope data:** A cleaned emission dataset is categorized into variables, such as scope 1, 2, and 3. Collected financial data, such as income statements and industry specific data is categorized and added to the datasets.
4. **AI modeling and training:** Oxari developed multiple AI models that identify distinct patterns in the datasets. We use these academically validated models to compute missing carbon emissions and ensure full data coverage.
5. **Result:** Our AI models compute missing emissions associated with a specific company, based on the company's unique profile. This output is derived from a weighted average of variables in our models, tailored towards the unique characteristics of a company, such as the sector and industry.

# Other

Our dataset supports sustainability disclosures, ESG reporting, and regulatory compliance initiatives. Hedge funds, venture capital, banks, impact consultants, and insurance companies leverage our data to evaluate investment opportunities and identify potential growth prospects across various industries.

Included are direct emissions (Scope 1), indirect emissions (Scope 2), and upstream and downstream emissions (Scope 3).

description:

Accern generates credit signals based on over a billion public news and social media content for companies, sectors and regions. Methodology:
Accern's credit NLP model has been trained on massive amounts of distressed company news and uses Accern's knowledge graph. For each passage, the model then computes a credit sentiment along with a number of other analytics (https://www.accern.com/adaptive-nlp).

harvested_at

title: Business Relationships
description:
Business relationships between public companies, subsidiaries and private companies that issue debt. title: Physical Risk

The dataset covers eight climate hazards, four scenarios and eight time periods for over 20,000 companies and over 870,000 asset locations.

The dataset includes:

-Company and asset level physical risk scores reflecting exposure to climate hazards across scenarios and time periods
-Company and asset level financial impact metrics reflecting the value of financial costs/losses projected due to changing climate hazard exposure for a given asset, expressed as a percentage of the asset value (% metric). Or for companies, the weighted average financial impact for all assets linked to the company, weighted by asset type weights
-Eight (8) physical risk hazards: Extreme Heat, Extreme Cold, Coastal Flooding, Wildfire, Drought, Fluvial Flooding, Tropical Cyclone and Water Stress
-Advanced climate physical hazard modeling leveraging CMIP6 climate models and proprietary modeling techniques, and covering four future climate change scenarios: Low (SSP1-2.6), Medium (SSP2-4.5), Medium-High (SSP3-7.0) and High (SSP5-8.5)

title: Market Derived Signals and Credit Default Swaps
description:
Timely information to help identify weakening credit for both rated and unrated entitles. The Market Derived Signals (MDS) and Credit Default Swaps (CDS) datasets provide an insight into credit risk through:

- MDS: Statistical measures based on a statistical model, the Market Derived Signals Model. The Market Derived Signals Model is the best-performing statistical model that evaluates CDS spreads in order to provide an early warning of potential credit changes and capture the market's daily view about a company's perceived risk.

- CDS: A contract between a seller and a buyer that obligates the seller, in exchange for a premium (spread) paid by the buyer, to insure the buyer against a loan default or other credit event. CDS are used for monitoring how the market views the credit risk across a wide range of companies,  financial institutions and banks.

The Market Derived Signals and Credit Default Swaps data provides timely information to help you identify weakening credit and fortify the analyst surveillance process for both rated and unrated entities by:
- Assessing, benchmarking and validating potential defaults, helping you build better risk protection into your business activities
- Capturing the latest market sentiment about a company's perceived risk, helping you engage in efficient credit risk-driven analysis
- Providing a gauge of the riskiness of corporate borrowers, helping you in speculation, hedging and arbitrage

description:
Company-level alignment with the Paris Agreement goal to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees C. The Trucost Paris Alignment data assesses company-level alignment with the Paris Agreement goal to limit global warming to well below 2°C from pre-industrial levels. The approach taken by Trucost is a transition pathway assessment, which examines the adequacy of emissions reductions over time required in order to meet either a 1.5°C or 2°C carbon budget.

Leverage this dataset to track your portfolios and benchmarks against the goal of limiting global warming to 1.5°C or 2°C climate change scenarios. The dataset allows users to identify the scale of reductions required by 2030 and beyond to meet the Paris Agreement goals.

This dataset includes:
- Coverage of 18,000 companies globally with a set of forward-looking analytical tools to quantify and track energy transition to a low carbon economy
- Forward-looking indicators over a medium-term time horizon, tracking the adequacy of company decarbonization across historical emissions and projected future emissions data
- Identification of companies and sectors that are compatible with a well below 2°C world

title: RatingsXpress®: Credit Ratings
description:
S&P Global Ratings data available by asset class, for credit and risk reporting, research and more. The RatingsXpress data provides access to S&P Global Ratings data for issuers and fixed income issues. Data is available by asset class, global issuers (corporations, banks, insurance, utilities), sovereigns, international public finance and government entities, structured finance (CDO, ABS, CMBS, RMBS), and US public finance (general obligations and revenue issuances).

You can utilize RatingsXpress to help you develop back testing models, conduct risk management benchmarks, test investment policy guidelines, perform analytical comparability, identify relative value, implement capital adequacy scenarios on user-defined criteria, and assess counterparty risk.

This dataset includes:

- Rating, CreditWatch, and Outlook assessments with corresponding dates, as well as asset class-specific terms and conditions
- Current and historical credit ratings with an entity and security-level data in one schema
- Coverage of nearly one million securities
- Identification of rated peers selected by S&P Global Ratings Analysts
- Near real-time, daily, or monthly frequencies

title: Preqin Alternative Asset Fund Performance
description:
In-depth data to asset classes covered in Private Equity, Real Estate, Hedge Funds, Infrastructure, and more. The Preqin dataset provides analytics and research on the alternative assets industry, including private equity, private debt, hedge funds, real estate, infrastructure and natural resources. You can utilize Preqin's data to support your daily activities including fundraising, investor relations, asset allocation, portfolio management, fund manager selection and business development.

This dataset includes:

- Fundraising & Dry Powder
- Fund performance metrics
- Profiles for 150,000+ funds, 51,000+ fund managers, and 22,000+ institutional investors
- Private capital market benchmark data for over 9,000 private capital funds
- Private Equity Relationships that commingle both Preqin and CIQ relationships
- Private Equity & Private Debt deals cross-reference data that enables to integrate multiple deals and MI/CIQ transaction level identifiers

title: S&P Dow Jones Indices via Xpressfeed
description:
Leading global indices from S&P Dow Jones Indices. The S&P Dow Jones Index dataset includes US and global historical equity benchmarking data, both at index level, as well as at their constituent level. Xpressfeed offers some of the leading global indices from S&P Dow Jones. Data is linked and fully integrated to all S&P Global Market Intelligence company and trading identifiers.

This dataset includes:
- US equity benchmarking products cover U.S. large-caps, mid-caps and small-caps. Among these are the S&P 500, S&P MidCap 400, and S&P SmallCap 600, which are widely recognized as leading indicators of U.S. equity market performance. The S&P 500 is the world's most-tracked index by AUM.
- The S&P Global 1200, the first real-time, tradable global equity index, captures approximately 70% of the world's market capitalization, offering investors efficient exposure to the world economy.
- The S&P Global Broad Market Index (BMI) series is a float adjusted index product, and is comprised of comprehensive, rules-based index series with a transparent and consistent methodology across all countries and includes approximately 10,000 stocks from 25 developed and 25 emerging markets.
- The S&P Dow Jones ESG Index Level is the first package of the upcoming ESG Index family. It includes Index level information for 199 ESG Indices and data for four unlicensed data items.
- Complimentary data includes daily price return and total return series data.
- Licensed data includes daily index market cap, index divisors, constituent weights, historical constituent names, identifiers, and corporate actions when available.

title: BitSight Security Ratings
description:
BitSight Security Ratings data describes a company's cybersecurity posture. The BitSight Security Ratings dataset provides insight into a company's cybersecurity posture, a measure of their risk, and transforms how companies manage security risk by using a data-driven, outside-in approach to rate a company's security effectiveness. You can utilize this dataset to monitor the risk of your business partners, insurance clients, or portfolio companies. Compare cyber risk trends and relative positioning of companies within an industry and create watch lists.

Scores are compiled and calculated using externally observable factors including open ports, exposed credentials, malware servers, file sharing, botnet infections, TLS/SSL configuration, and historical breaches.

This dataset includes:

- Global coverage of over 200,000 companies in the full universe
- Smaller target universes with 40,000+ companies available
- History back to 2015

title: 451 Research Datacenter KnowledgeBase
description:
Datacenter location and utilization data to support cloud services and critical infrastructure analysis. The 451 Research Datacenter KnowledgeBase dataset provides datacenter location, services, and utilization data to support cloud services, ESG, energy, media, and critical infrastructure analysis. Users will have access to a global database of 9,680+ colocation and wholesale datacenter facilities, covering more than 90 data points per facility.

Leverage this dataset to assess market and region energy as well as current and future demand from datacenters. Identify key datacenter suppliers in regional markets, assessing for likely expansion areas by region and identify new builds. Additionally, users can link data with existing Market Intelligence data for more comprehensive asset coverage.

This dataset includes:
- Datacenter location and ownership
- Capacity (space/power/racks)
- Leased/available capacity
- Certifications/capabilities

title: Economic Data
description:
Extensive historic and forecast coverage of global macroeconomic data. The Global Macroeconomic dataset includes comprehensive, timely and consistent data, robust forecasts and granular country/territory and industry data. Utilize this dataset to identify and optimize opportunities across the globe.

Datasets available include:
- Global Economic Forecast: Detailed medium- and-long term economic forecasts for 206 markets and regional aggregates
- Economic Analytics: Timely, historical macroeconomic and financial data provides extensive local coverage for 200+ markets from more than 800 sources
- US Economic Forecast: Detailed 10-year and 30-year economic forecast for the US with alternate scenarios
- US Regional Forecast: Short-term and long-term forecasts with extensive coverage by US region, state, metropolitan area, and county
- Canada Economic Forecast: In-depth Canadian national- and provincial-level forecasts
- Global Consumer Markets: Forecasts for 36 consumer spending categories, demographics, and income distribution across 112 markets
- Comparative Industry Service: Comparable forecasts including activity, sales, profits, costs, and risk across 105 industry sectors in 75 markets
- Global Construction Forecast: Comparable forecasts for the global construction industry covering residential and non-residential sectors across 74 markets
- Industry Forecast Monitor: Top-level supply and demand forecasts across major industries adds an industry dimension to our economic forecast
- Pricing and Purchasing Service: Used by global procurement departments to time buys, analyze supplier cost structures, and benchmark their purchasing performance

title: Securities Finance
description:
The Securities Finance dataset offers an expanded set of short interest-related data, published daily. The Securities Finance (Short Interest) dataset, originated from IHS Markit, includes stock loan availability and volume, short interest, and metrics reflecting the supply, demand and borrowing costs in the securities lending market, along with the flow of funds driving market prices.

With historical coverage from 2002, you can utilize this data to build asset allocation models and risk management processes. In addition, you can leverage this dataset when screening for possible investment candidates, assessing market sentiment, measuring lender liquidity of both equities and fixed income instruments, identifying the cost of borrowing for a security, or measuring the probability of short squeezes.

This dataset includes:

- Global coverage of securities finance short interest data in fixed
income and equity markets
- Daily and intraday updates from prime brokers, hedge funds, and lending agents with the ability to compare the data to the stock exchange aggregated short interest data that is provided on a bi-monthly, 10-day delay basis
- Timely information on offshore transactions and data from non-FINRA
registered firms

title: S&P CreditStats
description:
Provides financials adjusted by S&P Global Ratings' credit analysts. The S&P CreditStats dataset provides access to pre-and post-adjusted financial statement information to improve clarity, consistency, and comparability.

You can utilize this dataset to enhance your analysis of Corporations and Financial Institutions with consistent company-by-company and line-item-by-line-item financial statement data to support an evaluation of credit quality. You can also view financial information for US Public Finance Revenue Sources. S&P CreditStats is an efficient way of looking at these pre-adjusted and adjusted financials across periods.

Data is available for:

- Corporations with Period End Dates dating back to 2002
- Financial Institutions with Period End Dates dating back to 2006
- US Public Finance Revenue Sources with Period End Dates dating back to 2006

title: CreditPro®
description:
CreditPro® provides recovery analytics, trends, and performance data The CreditPro dataset provides a comprehensive picture of your credit risk exposures with access to authoritative default, transition and recovery data, and powerful database and analytic tools.

CreditPro provides tools to help you efficiently evaluate probabilities of default, track credits in transition, and analyze historical credit rating transitions, defaults and recoveries. This robust database and analytic tools helps you evaluate future default and ratings migration scenarios, and validate internal rating systems used for credit risk management purposes.

This dataset includes S&P Global Ratings default and ratings migration data covering:
- 17,000+ companies
- 130,000 securities
- 120,000 structured finance issues
- 160+ sovereign ratings across the globe

title: Dividend Forecasting
description:
Dividend forecasting contains forecast and historical dividend records The Dividend Forecasting dataset, originated from IHS Markit, contains independent dividend amount and date estimates for 28,000+ global stocks, ETFs and ADRs up to five years in the future.
A global team of 40 dividend analysts deliver precise forecasts of the size and timing of payments based on bottom-up fundamental research, the latest company news and insight from a proprietary advanced analytics model. Investment banks, hedge funds, quants and asset managers utilize these forecasts to confidently price derivatives, enhance their investment strategies and better understand dividend risk.
This dataset includes:
- Daily updates to forecasts that reflect the latest policy changes, company data and earnings releases
- Forecasts for up to 28,000+ stocks, including equity and fixed income ETFs and ADRs
- Precise forecasts for each dividend amount, ex-date, record and pay dates and supporting fields generated by trusted methodology
- Point-in-time forecasts for each dividend amount, ex-date, record date and pay dates
- Specialist commentary to help you discover trends and understand risk
- History going back to 2010

title: ETF Style Classifications
description:
ETF style classifications provide a tiered classification system which defines ETFs and ETNs The ETF Style Classifications dataset includes ETF classifications as well as over 40 standardized descriptive characteristics such as benchmark indices, expense ratio, leverage, and sector emphasis for over 12,000 global ETFs and ETNs.

Leverage ETF classifications to group ETFs by asset class, to screen based on specific characteristics such as benchmark index, leverage or inverse ETFs. This data can also be utilized for compliance purposes to identify ETFs that may restricted. The inclusion of not only the ETF classification but all the additional descriptive items allows for in-depth analysis into an ETF or ETN.

This dataset includes:
- ETF classifications based on asset class
- Geographic mandate
- Investment style
- Sector emphasis
- Management style
- Daily updates

title: RatingsXpress®: Research
description:
S&P Global Ratings credit research reports available in machine readable format. The RatingsXpress: Research dataset provides research reports published by S&P Global Ratings. Data is available by asset class, global issuers (corporations, banks, insurance, utilities), sovereigns, international public finance and government entities, structured finance (CDO, ABS, CMBS, RMBS), and US public finance (general obligations and revenue issuances).

Data scientists, research teams, and quantitative strategists interested in textual analysis and machine learning for investment, credit risk modeling, and developing sentiment/early warning models can utilize RatingsXpress: Research, S&P Global Ratings' digitized credit research.

Article types in this dataset include:  
- News
- Research Updates
- Full Analysis
- Summary Analysis
- Commentary

title: RatingsXpress®: Scores & Factors
description:
Provides transparency into the framework of the criteria used by S&P Global Ratings credit rating analysts The RatingsXpress®: Scores & Factors dataset provides transparency into how S&P Global Ratings analysts establish an Issuer Credit Rating.

By assessing the underlying business, financial, industry, and economic risk factors and assessments, plus the stand-alone credit profile, which drove an analyst's rating recommendation for an issuer, you can:
- Create meaningful financial benchmarks for internal risk models as a result of weakening support from the parent, affiliate, or related government
- Gain more insights into when the credit quality of an entity may be shifting by monitoring the underlying components of its credit rating
- Better differentiate between Issuers with the same rating by assessing a company's business risk profile, industry risk, and competitive position
- For banks adhering to Basel III regulations, decouple an Issuer's credit risk from any credit support provided to the entity

This dataset includes: 
- Historical coverage for corporations (CORP Score Group) dating back to 2017,  banks (BANK Score Group) dating back to 2018, insurers (INSURANCE Score Group) dating back to 2019, and sovereigns (SOV Score Group) dating back to 2018
- Historical coverage for Banking Industry & Country Risk Assessments (BICRA Score Group) dating back to 2019
- Available in span, daily or monthly frequencies

title: Country Risk
description:
Provides historic and forecast data including detailed overview on Country Risks Ratings and more. The Country Risk dataset, originated from IHS Markit, offers extensive historic and forecast data providing clients with a 360-degree perspective on Country Risks, ESG, Banking Sector Risk and News events related to political violence and political risk incidents.

This dataset includes:

- Country level risk ratings for 211 countries covering the full spectrum of geopolitical, security, economic, banking and investment risks. The scores provide a 12 month forward looking risk score with a directional outlook up to 3 years.
- The ESG risk scores system comprises 44 discrete factors that encompass the full spectrum of risks encountered by operators, covering sovereign-level Environmental, Social and Governance components of ESG. The scores represent IHS Markit's forecast for these risks over the coming 12 months.
- The Banking sector dataset includes high-quality, monthly updated data sourced from central banks, banking sector regulators and international organizations. Historical balance sheet, income statement, financial soundness indicators, and financial sector structure data for over 100 countries. 
- The Events database contains daily updated Intelligence Events (IEs) documenting the occurrence of political violence and political risk incidents. The events are systematically collected, and carefully structured data calibrated by formal intelligence collection requirements and are fully integrated into our wider intelligence processes and products.

- Liquidity metrics, such as the number of dealers quoting, with the size and the average size quoted
- 20+ years of price history

Investment Management firms, Investment Banks and Private Equity firms rely on MMD's pension fund data to target potential areas of growth within current investment portfolios, raise capital for new funds and target industry peers to generate revenue. title: SNL MediaCensus Broadband & Video
description:
Provides a granular view of the U.S. broadband and video landscape with subscriber, technology and speed data The MediaCensus Broadband & Video dataset allows users to discover the U.S. residential broadband and video landscape at a granular market level providing data to analyze subscriber trends by market and operator.

This dataset includes:
- MediaCensus Broadband & Video (by Zip & by County): This dataset provides a comprehensive analysis of entities within the U.S. broadband and video industry, and allows users to analyze subscriber market share, operator coverage, broadband speed, and technology type data. title: Municipal Bond Pricing
description:
Provides independent, transparent municipal bond pricing data to support trading, valuations and more. The Municipal Bond Pricing dataset, originated from IHS Markit, provides independent mark-to-market pricing with access to transparency metrics and liquidity scores on US Municipal bonds.

Our municipal pricing methodology incorporates the financial condition of each state and municipality, uses of proceeds and other factors at the issue level to drive movements in price. To support immediate price updates on instruments, our methodology incorporates unique market color fueled by parsing technology that extracts OTC pricing content from messages in real time along with data from the Municipal Securities Rule Making Board (MSRB). Our Municipal Bond pricing system has undergone a SOC 1 review.

This dataset includes:

- Pricing and analytics on 1 million Investment grade and High yield bonds
- Intraday price updates to support price discovery in the secondary market, valuation or to calculate net asset values of portfolios and assist in risk management
- Liquidity Score and additional transparency on number of dealer quoting, trades
- Historical coverage from 2011

title: Government, Supranational, Agency and Corporate (GSAC) Bond Pricing

Provides transparent pricing and liquidity data for more than 200,000 bonds  The Government, Supranational, Agency and Corporate (GSAC) Bond Pricing dataset, originated from IHS Markit, provides independent bid-offer pricing, analytics, and liquidity measures for over 200,000 global bonds. This dataset was built using a dynamic model that uses more than 15 million unique pricing quotes from a variety of sources.
Intraday and end-of-day price updates are used across organizations, starting from the front-office for price discovery on frequently quoted bonds, and in the middle- and back-office for risk management, valuations.

This dataset includes:
- Price updates available hourly for the full universe of over 200,000 bonds covering 70+ currencies
- Data on 70,000 money market instruments across 26 currencies
- Bonds Live, an additional service that is primarily used by trading desks, is available for almost 60,000 liquid securities

title: Commercial Prospecting

Provides commercial property data and UCC liens data combined with business listings across the U.S. The Commercial Prospecting dataset provides commercial property data and UCC liens data combined with business listings across the U.S. This dataset enables technology-driven lead generation and strong contact management, allowing you to easily screen Commercial Properties and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Liens in conjunction with Business Listings across the U.S to evaluate lending opportunities. - Business Listings: Provides details on 40M+ businesses across the U.S. detailing firmographics and geographic attributes, along with the Probability of Default for the respective NAICS industries on a state and county level.
- UCC Liens: Over 80M C&I Liens available via Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) filings for 45 states.

title: Machine Readable Broker Research
description:
Provides the value within equity research report for partner brokers. Machine Readable Broker Research unlocks the value within equity research reports by cleansing and parsing reports to deliver structured text from partner brokers for Natural Language Processing (NLP) analysis.
For each partner broker in the collection, a machine readable version of the brokers' published equity research is delivered through our existing feed channels. With a parsed, metadata tagged version of equity research, analysis can include:

- Focused research across report categories such as economic analysis, fixed income, portfolio/asset allocation, as well as event driven topics such as initiation of coverage, M&A, and public offerings
- Overweight articles published by brokers or analysts in their sectors of expertise with person ID's available for all publishers

- We are currently providing content from BNP Exane, Bank of Montreal, Liberum, Berenberg Bank, Macquarie Group, and CLSA

Machine Readable Broker Research is powered by Kensho Extract.

description:
Address Fabric is a current and comprehensive pre-geocoded list of all known addresses in the USA Consistent and correct location information is vital for conducting analysis with confidence while avoiding costly mistakes. Unique identifiers help you maintain your address and property databases, enrich address locations with contextual information, and perform spatial analytics. Address Fabric is the foundational data that provides the key for easily accessing this wealth of information.

Address Fabric is a current and comprehensive list of all known addresses in the United States. Each record is pre-geocoded to provide the most precise latitude and longitude coordinate location, including physical locations that are not deliverable by the postal service. Each record contains the street address, coordinate location, census information, and property details for that addressable location. Address genealogy known as parent/child relationships for primary and secondary addresses such as units, suites, and apartments are also included. Records are then assigned our unique identifier that can be used for data management and exchange, or appending enriched contextual information such as demographics, psychographics, property tax, and risk factors.

point

Over 40 postal attribute fields are also included to provide the detail needed to assist in utilizing ZIP Plus 4 data for internal processing and analysis. Additionally, Census block group codes, which include state, county, and tract codes, are provided for each ZIP Plus 4 record. A ZIP Code can represent one side of a street, a floor in a building, or a specific Post Office Box. The ZIP Code Sector (1234) represents a collection of addresses below the ZIP Code level. The ZIP Code Segment (1234) is more specific and always refers to a smaller set of addresses or a single address. In the case of PO Boxes, the ZIP segment is almost always the last two digits of the PO Box number. The four-digit ZIP Code extension is used by the United States Postal Service (USPS) to facilitate efficient mail handling and delivery. Data Sets - The ZIP Plus 4s product consists of two data sets - The base product table containing over 40 attribute fields. - An ‘unmatched’ file containing approximately 6 million ZIP+4 records that have coordinates representing either an interpolated ZIP+4, a ZIP+2, or a 5-digit ZIP centroid. The positional accuracy results for these records do not have the geographic elements required to meet Precisely’s quality criteria. However, these records are provided as they can still be used for more broad-based location matching and analysis. The unmatched ZIP+4 file has the same record layout as the base file but does not contain census tract, block group, or block values. Over 40 attribute fields include but are not limited to the following: - 5-digit ZIP Code - ZIP Plus 4 code extension - 5-digit ZIP Code and Plus 4 code extension - Point match type: 1 = ZIP+4 centroid, 2 = ZIP+2 centroid, 3 = 5-digit ZIP Code - Record type code: F- Firm ,G – General Delivery ,H – High-rise ,P – PO Box (and more) - 4-digit USPS carrier route ID - Street name - Street suffix abbreviation - Primary low number in address range - Primary high number in address range - Address primary odd/even code: O – Odd ,E – Even ,B – Both - Building or firm name. - ZIP Sector low number - ZIP Sector high number - ZIP Segment low number - ZIP Segment high number - LACS status code converted. - Government building indicator. - State FIPS Code - State abbreviation - County FIPS Code - County Name - Minor Civil Division code - CBSA Code - Congressional District number - Census block group code (state, county, tract, and block group codes) - Census block code (state, county, tract, block group and block codes) - Latitude - Longitude Coverage: San Francisco Bay Area, USA

Wildfire Risk is a scientific and up-to-date wildfire hazard and risk assessment data set for the United States.  This sample data set is limited to the Marin County, CA area. The model is based on Fire Behavior analysis and accounts for physical, climatic, and man-made variables including fuel type (vegetation) , fire intensity, ember impacts, burn probability, suppression factors, mitigation factors and high wind event areas as well as, insect impacts and community level attributes.
The net result is a set of uniquely generated FireShed polygons covering the United States with corresponding risk scores. There are three distinct fire environments covered by the model; Wildland, Intermix and Interface. Each of these areas has unique characteristics of structure density and fire behavior and therefore are evaluated separately to increase the models accuracy. All information is included at the address level using a unique identifier with additional proximity measurements to uncover further insight around structure specific risk.

Use cases
• Assess wildfire risk exposure using a model that uniquely addresses the varying characteristics of each landscape
• Maximize your bottom line by avoiding high risk areas while identifying pockets of opportunity in generally risky areas
• Understand wildfire risk at the property level rather than a macro region and price business accordingly
• Measure a property's proximity to high and very high wildfire zones.
• Visualize wildfire risk sheds for all 50 states

Product details

Wildfire Risk provides scores for the following hazard types:
• Wildland landscape risk (low structure density areas)
• Intermix landscape risk (moderate density areas with unique community attributes)
• Interface landscape risk (high density areas when embers are the main threat)
• Smoke - (areas that may have smoke and or evacuation impacts)
• Provides a wildfire model for all 50 states that scores the risk profile of every location from 0-49
• Includes a geo-enrichment file which appends all wildfire risk information to every affected address location using a unique identifier

title: StreetPro Traffic USA
description:
Provides typical traffic density for the complete road network, for every hour & day of the week StreetPro Traffic provides unique insight on typical traffic density for the complete road network, for every hour and day of the week. This includes the average amount of probe data received from our partner and third-party devices. As such, typical traffic density represents a sampled number of vehicles and not the total population of people driving on the road. StreetPro Traffic utilizes Floating Car Data (FCD) and GPS measurements coming from millions of connected sources to provide indicative traffic density by time of day and day of week. 

FCD is an innovative method of collecting data from navigation devices in vehicles. Example of probe devices include:
- smart phones
- dedicated navigation devices
- fleet management solutions

FCD contains information about localization, speed, time and direction of vehicle travel. Therefore, FCD primarily provides traffic information wherever there are vehicles traveling, not in non-vehicle areas. The data contains the aggregated results of all journeys driven with our partner automotive and GPS devices. The traveled road segments of each journey are identified on the road network, following the StreetPro Navigation Premium map. Then, an aggregation is completed over the different time group(s). This aggregation gives information, such as the traffic counts for each segment, the direction traveled and the hour and day. The data is the average of all data compiled in each specific time group and not the sum of the data.

This collection of historical traffic information provides valuable insight into the traffic situation on the road network throughout the day. StreetPro Traffic data consists of data aggregated over past 6 months preceding the release date. 

The results represent all road classes open for traffic. However, traffic counts with hour resolution are only provided when probe data volumes are sufficient. Otherwise, the only traffic counts provided are per week or weekdays. In order to provide a continuous road network, road elements without probe data have also been provided within the product.

For customers wishing to understand the underlying road network attribution, StreetPro Traffic can also be joined to StreetPro Navigation Premium.

description:
Represents the area served by a particular USPS mail carrier. Boundaries follow roads for accuracy. The Carrier Route Boundaries product represents the area served by a particular USPS mail carrier. Using multiple data sources, Precisely creates boundaries that follow roads, both for accuracy and visual appeal. Our proprietary process captures residential and business routes with the resulting product being a great resource for direct marketers. Other advantages include:

•	Use of multiple data feeds, including USPS data, to ensure completeness
•	CASS-certifiable data imported each month;
•	Rigorous linkage of ZIP+4 data to every US street segment;
•	Segment scores based on match rates;
•	Areas are incorporated cleanly, without the “fake accuracy” of jagged fence-posting used by other companies.

There are 5 primary tables in the product:

Carrier Route Boundaries - provides latitude/longitude coordinates for the vertices of carrier route polygons. Point-type carrier routes are not included in this version.

Carrier Route Centroids - includes all carrier routes, one record per, including point-type routes such as PO Boxes and others for which an accurate boundary cannot be defined. If possible, PO Box carrier routes are located at a post office’s physical location; otherwise, these routes appear at the ZIP centroid. If a point carrier route is not a PO Box, we attempt to place it at the centroid of the street segment where we have the best match; otherwise, we place it at the ZIP centroid.

ZIP Code Boundaries, ZIP Code Centroids, ZIP Code Alternate Names - 5-digit ZIP Code boundaries and centroids are included with the Carrier Route Boundaries product in a separate set of files. The ZIP Codes have the same currency as, and their boundaries align with, their respective carrier routes.  The ZIP Code alternate names provides all names associated with a particular ZIP Code in a separate table for faster geocoding and better hit rates in the main ZIP Code boundary file.

title: Global ETF Data
description:
Classifications, Holdings and Key Stats Data on Global ETF's CFRA has three separate categories of ETF data; holdings, classifications and key stats data.

The classifications and reference data we capture, consists of ~90 columns that give detailed information about an ETF. These granular details include asset class, expense ratio, index name, index weighting scheme, smart beta type and specific investment objectives, and are great for everything from helping our clients understand the characteristics of an ETF, to generating meaningful peer groups. 

Our holdings data, details all the constituent securities in each ETF with names, identifiers, and the weights for each security to give great transparency, and allowing our clients to fully understand the drivers behind risk or opportunity in an investment.

To complete the dataset, we collect key ETF performance data, including prices, NAV’s, flows, returns and much more, all of which is collected and published for multiple time periods. 

Our data is available right now for over + 9,500 unique ETF’s globally. NB this universe will vary slightly over time as new ETF’s are bought to market and others are delisted.

title: Comscore Media Consumption – TV Viewership
description:
Monthly TV viewership insights spanning network, genre, daypart and ad exposure Comscore’s TV viewership data provides a rich set of data based on granular TV viewership insights. Powered by Comscore’s expansive TV footprint that captures viewership from 75 million TV screens in over 40 million homes, measuring linear viewership of 1 in 3 US households. Comscore passively collects second-by-second TV set-top-box (STB) return path data sourced from leading MVPD partnerships and uses this viewership to provision our data for targeting and analytics. Comscore creates the largest single-source cross-platform dataset by matching deterministic STB data with our digital data in a privacy-compliant manner, leveraging our patented machine learning device graph. Within this dataset, we identify households exposed to the target viewing criteria as a seed set, utilizing that information with thousands of other potential attributes to create sophisticated statistical models to score user-IDs based on TV viewership behaviors. Easily join Comscore TV viewership data with your internal data for valuable analytics and to optimize campaign performance.

title: Foursquare Ready-to-Use Audiences - US only
description:
This data set contains consumer device IDs segmented by behavioral interest and place visitation activity. This data set contains consumer device IDs segmented by behavioral interest and place visitation activity. These 688 audience segments are designed by Foursquare location experts and reflect the most popular targeting segments requested by marketers. We publish revisions to this data set on a bi-monthly cadence.

We create audiences using a combination of mobile device geolocation data, consumer online interest data, our proprietary, global Places dataset and proprietary technologies. We source mobile device geolocation data from a variety of premium partners, including via our own SDKs, and then validate that data using our proprietary Location Validation technology in order to remove those signals that are of insufficient quality. Then, our proprietary snap-to-place technology determines the specific place that the mobile device user visited by evaluating hundreds of attributes (such as movement detection, business density, popularity of place, hours of operation, time of day, day of week, and frequency of visitation) in order to attach it to a specific point of interest within our proprietary Places dataset. The validated place visit is then added to our device dataset. Finally, mobile devices are classified into related ready-to-use Audiences.

- consumer_id: MAID (IDFA or Android ID)
- id_type: Enumerated value indicating whether the consumer_id is an IDFA or an Android ID
- segment_ids: Array of FDC codes representing the segments within the given Data Set that the consumer_id belongs to

title: CSRHub ESG (Environment, Social, Governance) Fast Start
description:
ESG ratings for 20,000 entities with ~12 years data: Environment, Governance, Community and Employees. The core of our dataset: 20,000 entities with overall ratings and four category scores (Environment, Community, Governance and Employees).  Includes >90% of world market cap (publicly traded entities), plus hundreds of large private entities, and more than 155 government entities. Monthly history goes back about 12 years (when it is available--many of these companies have only recently begun sharing enough ESG data to become rated).

More than 850 ESG sources contributed the data we use to find the consensus view of these entities. Our big data model normalizes, maps, and weights 11,500 different sustainability-related indicators that touch on carbon emissions, water use, leadership ethics, diversity, philanthropy, training, compensation, and transparency.

Our full data set covers 50,000 entities and offers an additional twelve indicators underneath the four described above.  It reaches back to December 2008 and includes entities that have merged, gone out of business, etc., since the inception of our dataset.  We offer the full data set under different terms (please reach out to support@csrhub.com if you are interested in the full data set).  Our full data set also includes a number of alternate company names, the company web site address, address, industry, and description information.

The Trial data set is for only the current components of the Dow Jones 30 index.

Fields for both Trial and Production data sets are:
- CSRHUB_ID (invariant identifier for each entity)
- COMPANY_NAME (name of the entity)
- ISIN (the ISIN for the entity, available for > 90% of the data set)
- TICKER (the ticker for the entity, available for >90% of the data set)
- INDUSTRY_DESC (an industry description based on a modified NAICS code)
- DJ30TAG (is the entity a member of the current Dow Jones 30 Index?)
- COMMUNITY (rating for product, philanthropy, community development and other external social issues)
- EMPLOYEES (rating for diversity, compensation, safety, training, and other internal social issues)
- ENVIRONMENT (rating for climate change, resource management, environmental reporting, recycling, and other environment issues)
- GOVERNANCE (rating for board, leadership, transparency and other governance issues)
- RATING_DATE (the month for which the ratings are valid)
- RATING_STATUS (Y = Fully rated; P = Partially rated; only fully rated companies are included in the data set)

Example Use Cases:
Corporate Managers:
- Benchmark against your peers
- Improve stakeholder communication
- Pinpoint ESG reporting gaps
- Review your supply chain
- Uncover ESG business opportunities
Investors & Analysts:
- Screen your investment universe
- Back test to find material ESG indicators
- Share your ESG strategy with clients
- Engage with companies
- Improve asset owner reporting
Consultants & Advisors:
- Expand your ESG expertise
- Find and focus on the best reporting strategy
- Propose innovations and drive change
- Communicate with all levels of management
- Build client ESG knowledge

For each entity, we estimate an overall rating at an accuracy of plus or minus one point, at a 95% confidence interval. We then offer Environment, Governance, Employee, and Community ratings. (We split "Social" into an outside and inside signal.) The FastStart production set includes the company name, its Ticker, and its ISIN (when we have Tickers and ISINs available).

Ratings range from 0 to 100 with few scores below 10 or above 90.  The midpoint of each distribution is around 50 but the distribution may be skewed.  Ratings are provided as an integer (no decimal places) in this product (up to four decimal places of accuracy are available in the full CSRHub product).

title: Movement - Global Daily Activity Index (Commercial)
description:
Anonymous, aggregated, daily mobility data for every 100m grid tile in supported global markets Mapbox Movement is a privacy-forward dataset of device density, activity, and movement over time drawn from 700M+ users and 45,000+ different mobile apps globally contributing 20B+ live location updates daily. The dataset captures significant driving and non-driving mobile device activity aggregated into geographic tiles of 100-meter resolution (approx. 1 city block) and administrative boundaries (states/counties). Mapbox Movement dataset provides a high-definition view of how, where, and when people move through a city or specific geography.

The counts are normalized and low-volume areas are excluded from the data to protect user privacy. No PII attributes are included in this data set. This data cut is baselined using January 2020 as a reference period.

Data schema:
- geography: ID of the zoom-level 18 tile (or Boundary ID)
- xlon, xlat: coordinates of the grid tile centroid
- bounds: bounding box of the grid tile
- activity_index_total: normalized activity factor
- activity_index_driving: normalized activity factor filtered by vehicle modality
- agg_day_period: date (local time)

Example Use Case:
Use the historical and daily-updating activity index to compare movement levels around 2 different locations to understand and compare mobility levels as a proxy for commercial demand over time. Are stores in a certain area underperforming relative to competitors? Are there “hotspots” of activity where new sites should be located?

Sample Data:
Sample data for various geographies may be accessed through the respective Standard Tile listings.

Requesting Access:
Upon requesting access to this data, Mapbox will reach out to discuss the requested geographies and licensing options. Once a license has been purchased, data will be made available through Secure Shares.
