title: US Equities Short Share Volume Data
description:
Consolidated TRF/ADF Daily Short Sale Volume data for trades in exchange-listed securities. Purchase with a sample includes the most recent month of daily consolidated TRF/ADF Daily Short Sale Volume data which combines the volume for trades in exchange-listed securities reported to the TRFs and the ADF.  


The Short Sale Files do not—and are not intended to—equate to bi-monthly reported short interest position information. The short interest data reflects short positions held by market participants at a specific moment in time on two discrete days each month, while the Daily File reflects the aggregate volume of trades executed as short sales on each trade date.

Some market participants mistakenly conclude that the bi-monthly short interest data is understated because the Daily File reflects short sale volume that is much larger than what is reported as short interest. However, short interest data reflects short positions held by market participants at a specific moment in time on two discrete days each month, while the Daily File reflects the aggregate volume of trades executed as short sales on each trade date. Therefore, while the two data sets are related (i.e., short sale volume may ultimately result in a reportable short interest position), they are not necessarily correlated.

For example, if a firm sells short 1,000 shares of security ABCD, then purchases 1,000 shares of ABCD later the same day, the short sale volume in the Daily File will include the 1,000 shares that were sold short. Because the firm sold short and purchased an equivalent number of shares that day, it did not establish or accumulate a short position in ABCD; thus, its short sale has no impact on the reported short interest in ABCD.

title: Climate Projections from Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6)
description:
Monthly projections under different scenarios of temperature, humidity, precipitation, and snow to year 2100 Pollen has reprocessed publicly-available data from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6), which is an international collaboration of dozens of climate labs that seeks to predict what will happen to the Earth's climate between now and the year 2100.  If you've seen a simple graph in, say, The New York Times of how hot the Earth will be in a "business as usual" scenario vs "best case scenario", then you have already seen this data, except aggregated into a simple, global mean.

There's so much more than just global mean temperatures available, though.  The scientific community has created projections for hundreds of variables (snow coverage, precipitation, etc) in resolutions as small as 100km squares and in time steps as small as daily, projected out into the year 2100.  We've reprocessed a useful subset of this data so, instead of wrestling with its original, hard to use, Earth science specific format (netCDF), you can query it easily with SQL, directly in Snowflake, instead.

See https://www.pollen.io/snowflake/ for more information.

Samples/Tables Included:
- Monthly simulated "historical" climate data from 1850-2015
- Monthly projected climate data from 2015-2100 based on different potential carbon emission scenarios (called Representative Concentration Pathways and Shared Socioeconomic Pathways)
- All of the above for temperature, humidity, precipitation, and snow area coverage (with more on  the way)
- Also, for convenience, a table of shapefiles of US states, for easy joining by state name
- Also, a table of all the Creative Commons licensing information you'll need to stay compliant with the original data's attribution requirements.

Fields Included (see also: https://www.pollen.io/snowflake/actual_variables.html)
- GIS-style polygon defining the 100km square on Earth
- square surface area of geographic polygon (for taking weighted averages)
- source (i.e. which climate model)
- experiment (i.e. best case vs worst case vs middle of road)
- month and year
- temperature in F and C
- precipitation in mm/day and in/day
- specific and relative humidity
- snow area coverage

Please note at all of the above (even for historical dates) are simulations, not actual, direct measurements.

Example Use Case: 
Join your customer addresses and use temperature projections to see which users in your own customer list are going to experience the most summer temperature change between now and 2050.  Use temperature projections to see which US states will experience the most heat stress during harvest season over 10, 20, 30 and 50 year intervals.  Snow projections to see if you can still go skiing on Mount Shasta in December after the year 2040.

title: Overture Maps - Admins
description:
Named localities in the real world including settlements, cities, regions, provinces and countries.  The Overture admins theme includes entities that describe named localities in the real world including settlements, cities, regions, provinces and countries. 

Admin Types:

1. Administrative boundary:
An Administrative Boundary is typically an officially defined border between two Administrative Localities. In light of geopolitical issues, some Administrative Boundaries can represent standalone disputed or treaty lines and therefore do not coincide with the border of an Administrative Locality. The Administrative Boundary and two Administrative Localities do no share common geometry. 

2. Locality:
Localities are named, and typically populated, areas. Administrative Localities represent countries and hierarchical subdivisions of countries. Every Administrative Locality has a valid adminLevel property set, defining its position in the subdivision hierarchy. All Administrative Localities at sub-country level must have a contextId property containing the GERS ID of the feature's parent Administrative Locality. title: Overture Maps - Transportation
meta_info: Mapping and geospatial visualizations,Location Planning,Location Geocoding
description:
Collection of features and attributes that describe the infrastructure and conventions of how people travel. Overture's transportation layer is the collection of features and attributes that describe the infrastructure and conventions of how people and objects travel around the world. Transportation data includes highways, footways, cycleways, railways, ferry routes and public transportation.

1. Segments:

Segments are paths which can be traveled by people or things. Segment geometry represents the center-line of a path which may be traveled. Segment properties describe both the physical attributes (e.g. road surface and width) and non-physical attributes (e.g. access restriction rules) of that path. Two Segments are physically connected if a common Connector is referenced from the connectors property of both Segments. Where this occurs, both Segment geometries must contain the common Connector's coordinates. A physical connection between Segments indicates that it may be possible to travel from one segment to the next at the connected location, provided the Segment properties do not indicate a restriction, such as a turn restriction, which would prevent the transition in a particular case. Conversely, two segments are not physically connected—even if their geometries intersect—if they do not share a Connector in common.


2. Connectors:

Connectors create physical connections between Segments. Connectors help define the topology of the transportation network by defining points of physical connection between two or more Segments.

title: Return On Investment of U.S. Colleges
description:
Detailed location, cost, earnings, debt, and ROI data for colleges and universities in the U.S. Description:

This unique dataset provides directory (name, location, control/sector), enrollment (undergraduate, Pell), cost (tuition, net price, and cost of attendance), performance (retention, graduation), debt (loan, repayment), earnings (median income, 25th and 75th percentile), and return-on-investment (ROI) calculations for 4,125 colleges and universities in the United States. With access, users can:

1. Search for and locate every college and university in the U.S. and see the costs of attendance overall, including for in-state versus out-of-state students.

2. View various performance metrics for each institution, including retention and graduation rates, debt/loan repayment or default rates, and the percent of students awarded federal Pell Grants and federal student loans.

3. Observe the median debt of graduates upon completion and the estimated monthly loan payment for borrowers from each institution.

4. View the mean and median earnings of graduates from those institutions at 10 years after entry, including the 25th and 75th earnings percentiles, as well as the proportion of graduates making more than $25,000 per year.

5. Observe the estimated cumulative earnings after enrolling up to 10 years, as well as the estimated cumulative earnings of a high-school graduate in that same state (i.e., to view a college-earnings benefit).

6. Access Vantage Point's return-on-investment calculations for each college and university (i.e., comparing the college benefit to the investment required to attend that college).

This proprietary dataset is developed by Vantage Point's leading education and data scientists and is powered by annual college-level data from the U.S. Department of Education.

As one of the first and most comprehensive datasets on college ROI, this dataset provides essential information for students and families, policymakers, institutional and program administrators, and workforce leaders seeking to make informed decisions on investments and partnerships in higher education.

Topics Covered:
- Colleges and universities in the U.S.
- Cost of attendance (tuition, fees, net price)
- Debt (mean/median, repayment rate, median monthly payment)
- Earnings 10 years after enrollment (median, 25th/75th percentile)
- Return-on-Investment (10 years, compared to high school graduate)

Household-level continuous scoring system; ranks estimated consumer capacity to spend, save or invest Affluence Index™ is a household-level continuous scoring system that measures and ranks estimated consumer spending power, so marketers can better segment, differentiate, and target customers and prospects with the likely capacity to spend, save or invest. 

Affluence Index™ can more accurately predict spending because it incorporates wealth information derived from multiple sources, including summary factors produced from our proprietary database of consumer investable assets. 

It provides a household-level continuous score ranging from 1 to 1000, with a rating of 1000 representing the highest estimated level of spending power. Scores can be appended to any customer or prospect file to help identify and target new customers and prospects by their spending potential.

Affluence Index™ can be bundled with other financial capacity measures such as Income360®, Ability to Pay Index™, or Spending Power™ to provide an even more granular view of household disposable income. 

Fields Included: 
- ZIP Code
- ZIP+4 Code
- Affluence Index Score

Detailed Credit Variables (Basic Package): Estimates of household credit behavior provided at the neighborhood level used to differentiate households based on their likely credit availability, needs, and usage. It enables financial services marketers and analysts to gain insight on all types of credit usage including mortgages, HELOC, HELoans, bank cards, retail cards, student loans, auto loans, and other non-mortgage loans.

Risk Scores (Full Package*):  CreditStyles Pro offers aggregated Equifax Risk Scores for households within a micro-neighborhood, enabling firms to reduce risk and better target and service their customers and prospects. The risk scores predict households’ likely future credit behavior based on previous behavior as well as compared to credit files that have had similar characteristics under similar conditions. Equifax risk score models typically assign higher scores to consumers who exhibit a likelihood of high, or satisfactory, credit performance and lower scores to consumers who exhibit a likelihood of low, or unsatisfactory performance.

Intent Indicators (Full Package*):  Intent Indicators offer indexed measures that identify households’ likely propensity to acquire new credit or to inquire or respond about a new line of credit. Marketers can use Intent Indicators for both offline ITA marketing and online digital ad display marketing in order to better identify households that are likely seeking a specific credit product.

title: Financial Durability Measures
meta_info: Customer Acquisition,Subscriber Acquisition and Retention,Risk Analysis,Market Analysis,Quantitative Analysis
description:
Available Score and Index measures provide a holistic view of a household’s likely financial resilience Financial durability isn’t always obvious. Two consumers may have the same credit risk profile, but differing levels of financial durability because traditional credit scores don’t tell you what’s in a consumer’s financial wallet. Financial Durability measures provide unique insight into households’ likely financial resilience — meaning how likely a household is able to keep spending, plus meet current and future financial obligations, even when under financial stress.

The Financial Durability model from Equifax provides an indicator of financial resilience by analyzing the intersection of multiple financial capacity measures:

Affluence — based on a foundation of anonymous invested assets
Estimated total household income — based on income from wages, assets, business, and retirement funds
Spending power — discretionary funds available to spend, save, or invest, after accounting for fixed expenses of life
Aggregated credit — such as credit utilization and delinquencies

These household-level scoring measures are offered in two formats for maximum flexibility: 
Financial Durability Score™ - provides a 1 to 5 score, with a 5 representing households that are the most financially resilient. 
Financial Durability Index™ - provides a more granular 1 to 1000 rating, with a higher rating representing households that are more financially resilient. 

These Financial Durability measures can be used for non-FCRA applications across the customer lifecycle, enabling marketers and risk managers to differentiate consumers for acquisition efforts, inform pre-collections strategies, assist with treatment prioritization for delinquent accounts, and increase recovery for accounts in collections.

Financial Durability Score or Index can be bundled with our other financial capacity measures such as Income360, Affluence Index™ or Spending Power™ to provide an even more granular view of household financial health and resilience.

Fields Included:
Zip+4
DPC
Financial Durability Score numeric value (1 - 5)
Financial Durability Index numeric value (1 - 1000)

Economics are at the heart of every household purchase decision. Income, credit capacity, spending power and other financial measures play a significant role in consumer behavior. Economic Cohorts is a household-level marketing segmentation system that helps marketers better understand and communicate more relevant consumer offers by providing additional insights into likely economic capacity, behaviors and demographics of target households. It enables marketers to answer questions such as:
 
How can I determine the product preference and household economics that drive the spending decisions of my prospects and customers?
How can I best combine my customer data with household economics data to improve my marketing ROI?
 
Economic Cohorts is the first segmentation system to provide marketers a complete picture of the customer wallet in combination with all of the key demographic, behavioral and lifestyle attributes you expect from a first-class consumer segmentation system. It classifies all U.S. households into one of 71 different household types called “clusters” or “segments” based on a multi-dimensional framework including: 
 
Economic capacity — estimated income, spending, credit capacity and usage, and ability to pay
Behaviors and characteristics — lifestyles, media, channels, age, demographics, psychographics, home ownership, and urbanicity
 
Economic Cohorts is built on a foundation of proprietary economic data derived from multiple sources, including the Equifax proprietary database of consumer investable assets, whereas other segmentation solutions rely on survey and/or Census-based data as the primary driver of their clustering methodology. Equifax Economic Insights data also more accurately identifies affluent households.
 
Economic Cohorts can be bundled with our other financial capacity measures such as Ability to Pay Index™, Income360, Affluence Index™, Spending Power™, CreditStyles Pro, and Financial Durability Index to provide an even more granular view of household financial health and resilience.

title: Financial Durability Measures (Demo/Sample)
meta_info: Market Analysis,Risk Analysis,Quantitative Analysis,Subscriber Acquisition and Retention
description:
Available Score and Index measures provide a holistic view of a household’s likely financial resilience Financial durability isn’t always obvious. Two consumers may have the same credit risk profile, but differing levels of financial durability because traditional credit scores don’t tell you what’s in a consumer’s financial wallet. Financial Durability measures provide unique insight into households’ likely financial resilience — meaning how likely a household is able to keep spending, plus meet current and future financial obligations, even when under financial stress.

The Financial Durability model from Equifax provides an indicator of financial resilience by analyzing the intersection of multiple financial capacity measures:

Affluence — based on a foundation of anonymous invested assets
Estimated total household income — based on income from wages, assets, business, and retirement funds
Spending power — discretionary funds available to spend, save, or invest, after accounting for fixed expenses of life
Aggregated credit — such as credit utilization and delinquencies

These household-level scoring measures are offered in two formats for maximum flexibility: 
Financial Durability Score™ - provides a 1 to 5 score, with a 5 representing households that are the most financially resilient. 
Financial Durability Index™ - provides a more granular 1 to 1000 rating, with a higher rating representing households that are more financially resilient. 

These Financial Durability measures can be used for non-FCRA applications across the customer lifecycle, enabling marketers and risk managers to differentiate consumers for acquisition efforts, inform pre-collections strategies, assist with treatment prioritization for delinquent accounts, and increase recovery for accounts in collections.

Financial Durability Score or Index can be bundled with our other financial capacity measures such as Income360, Affluence Index™ or Spending Power™ to provide an even more granular view of household financial health and resilience.

Fields Included:
Zip+4
DPC
Financial Durability Score numeric value (1 - 5)
Financial Durability Index numeric value (1 - 1000)

title: Unified ID 2.0: Advertiser Identity Solution
description:
Maximize opportunity by converting your CRM data to Unified ID 2.0. NOTE: If you are an existing client of The Trade Desk and are interested in this solution, please include your Partner and Advertiser IDs issued by The Trade Desk in the message field of the data request.

With reduced reliance on the third-party cookie in the addressable advertising industry, Unified ID 2.0 (UID2) enables deterministic identity for advertising opportunities on the open internet without exposing sensitive directly identifying information (DII). As an advertiser, you can join purchase and exposure data tied to UID2s, thus optimizing audience targeting on the open internet in near-real time, while protecting consumer privacy.

With the Unified ID 2.0 identity solution you can map user DII data to UID2s, thus allowing UID2-enabled participants to use your first-party data to run more efficient advertising campaigns without revealing any DII.

To protect UID2s from unauthorized access, UID2-enabled participants must encrypt the UID2s they share with other UID2 participants into UID2 tokens. With the Unified ID 2.0 identity solution you can encrypt the UID2s into UID2 tokens before sharing with other parties and then, when receiving UID2 tokens, decrypt them into raw UID2s.

The UID2 Share reveals only essential data and functions needed for you to perform the following UID2-related tasks:

- Map email addresses, phone numbers, or their hashes to the corresponding UID2s and the second-level salt bucket IDs.
- Check the last salt update time for each second-level salt bucket ID.
- Encrypt UID2s into UID2 tokens.
- Decrypt UID2 tokens to extract the enclosed UID2s.

title: Data Onboarding
description:
Onboard first-party and third-party data to Magnite for activation. The Magnite Data Onboarding listing allows you to onboard your first-party or third-party data for activation within Magnite SSPs.  The following provides a step-by-step approach for Clients and Data Partners to onboard their data into Magnite. This listing currently supports onboarding data for activation on Magnite Streaming.

To get started, click the request button to email the Magnite Snowflake admin team with more information on the data you want to onboard. Please include:
 * Your company name
 * A point of contact and email address
 * The type of data you want to onboard (first-party/3rd party) 
 * The data size
 * The number of user profiles
 * The average number of segments per profile
 * Expected frequency of updates. 
 * Expected size of updates.
 * The region where data is located. Note: Magnite requires data to be stored in US-east-1.

A member of our admin team will review the request.  Once the request is approved, Magnite will share our target Snowflake account name so you can begin sharing data views with Magnite.

Segment Membership and Taxonomy Table Requirements. 
Magnite requires a segment membership and taxonomy table for data onboarding. The following outlines the requirements for each table. 

Segment Membership Table Requirements 
Field | Data type | Required | Optional | Definition
StorageId | VARCHAR(255) | Required | first-party ID,  device ID, or IP
IdType | VARCHAR(36) | Required | First Party ID, IDFA, RIDA, TIFA, AAID/GAID, or IP
SegmentId | VARCHAR(36) | Required | Required even if a publisher and advertiser plan to maintain one master list. One Segment per row.
Active | BOOLEAN | Required | TRUE or FALSE. A user is opted-out when set to FALSE.
UpdateTimestamp | TIMESTAMP | Required | Timestamp of the update to Magnite.

Taxonomy Table Requirements
Field | Data type | Required | Optional | Definition
ClientName | VARCHAR(255) | Required | Data Provider or Publisher or Advertiser Name
AccountId | VARCHAR(36) | Required | Magnite Account ID associated with the client. (This is where the segment needs to go within Magnite.)
DataShareSettings | VARCHAR(36) | Required | Values are Public or Private.
SegmentId | VARCHAR(36) | Required | Segment ID(s) provided in the segment membership table.
SegmentName | VARCHAR(255) | Required | Name of the segment.
SegmentDescription | VARCHAR(255) | Optional | Notes/metadata on the segment. 
SegmentCPM | DOUBLE | Optional | Cost of the segment. This is USD and cents.
Platform | VARCHAR(255) | Required | Magnite Streaming. Eventually, additional platforms will be supported.
Active | BOOLEAN | Required | TRUE or   FALSE. Related to segment status.
UpdateTimestamp | TIMESTAMP | Required | Timestamp of update to Magnite.

Data Share Requirements
1. To ensure data is in the correct format, please run the code snippet in the SQL Query section of this listing before sharing data (https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vR2GuqGfhCHpXodO6vP-I4CP4YE2y5DXxu552b_OPSKU-0rOI_Znb8WdEabgSw2PncxAIs9QhjoY1-j/pub)
2. A stream (change tracking) on the view must be enabled. For more information on this, see https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/streams-manage or contact Magnite for more information.
3. To make the view accessible to Magnite, please create a share of each table and grant privileges to the shared objects using our target Snowflake account name.

Magnite Data Ingestion
Updates to data shares are checked and ingested into Magnite daily.

title: MBS Loan Level Historical Data: Full Access
meta_info: Risk Analysis,Mortgage Prepayment Analysis,Mortgage Bank Prepayment Analysis,Mortgage Market Trends
description:
Enhanced and Normalized Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae Loan Level Data for the MBS Universe


RiskSpan’s MBS Loan Level Historical Data includes the entire universe of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae Mortgage Back Securities, covering the entire scope of this $9T market. Data represents the entire available history of loan level performance data from each Agency. RiskSpan has normalized the data across Agencies, making cross-market analysis a seamless process. Derived and enhanced data are included in the offering; key derived fields include current coupon, refinance incentive, current loan-to-value ratio, original specified pool designation, and normalized seller and servicer names.


MBS traders are able to use this data to track historical prepayment speeds, uncover trading opportunities that generate relative value, and build, enhance, or calibrate prepayment models.


Loan originators can use the data to track their performance against the market, allowing them to potentially demonstrate preferred performance to generate premiums during the issuance process.


Two core datasets are included in the offering—One includes the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac universes combined (with a field ‘Agency’ to differentiate) and the other includes the Ginnie Mae universe. Data infields cover 40+ borrower, loan, property, and performance attributes.

title: Gain a cyclical insight into the BDC investment space with this comprehensive dataset
description:
Consolidated Schedule of Investments extracted from 10-Q filings With this data, companies can track the investments by firms registered with the 
SEC as Business Development Companies to gain insight into investment trends, competitive intelligence and market sentiment. For instance, 21 BDCs came online and reported their first schedule of investments in 2023! 

This dataset includes records from the Consolidated Schedule of Investments tables published within 10-Q filings from the Edgar SEC.gov database for all companies that are registered as Business Development Companies (BDC). 

A Business Development Company (BDC) is a type of publicly traded private equity firm that provides capital to small and mid-sized businesses, often in the form of loans or equity investments. These companies operate with the intention of generating income from debt interest or capital appreciation, making them an attractive vehicle for income-seeking investors. BDCs are regulated by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and are required to distribute at least 90% of their taxable income as dividends to investors.

The Consolidated Schedule of Investments is a comprehensive report that BDCs file with the SEC on a quarterly basis and publish on the EDGAR platform. This document outlines in detail the portfolio investments made by the BDC. The information provided typically includes:

The name of the portfolio company
The type of security (equity, secured debt, unsecured debt, etc.)
The industry or sector of the portfolio company
The date of the investment
The cost of the investment
The fair value of the investment
The percentage of net assets each investment represents
Interest rates and maturity dates for loans

This detailed breakdown provides transparency and allows investors to understand the risk profile, investment strategy, and overall performance of the BDC. The data contained in the Consolidated Schedule of Investments offers valuable insights for potential investors, financial analysts, and researchers studying the BDC industry or the specific sectors in which the BDCs invest.

title: CMBS Special Servicing Commentary
meta_info: Risk Analysis,Asset Valuation,Market Analysis,Data Quality and Cleansing
description:
Extracted for SEC.gov EDGAR 10-D Filings This dataset contains data about CMBS loans in special servicing from Edgar Form 10-D filings for 100+ CMBS deals across 1000+ filings (monthly). The earliest reported period is 2023-03-02. The dataset is updated daily to capture all future 10-D filings as they are published in Edgar.

The SEC Form 10-D is a fundamental tool for financial transparency, primarily designed to disclose essential information regarding Asset-Backed Securities (ABS) and their performance to the investors. Filed monthly, it provides a comprehensive account of the pool's assets, payment priorities, and the distribution of the cash flow amongst investors. Its meticulous detail aids in assessing the overall performance of the ABS, ensuring analysts in Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) and Commercial Real Estate (CRE) fields can make informed investment decisions.

The schema includes Edgar identifiers and timestamps along with the structured fields scraped from the html filings:

- FILING_ID: Unique identifier for each SEC 10-D filing.
- FILING_DATE: The date the 10-D filing was submitted.
- ACTUAL_BALANCE: The outstanding balance on the loan.
- APPRAISAL_VALUE: The most recent property valuation amount.
- DSCR (Debt Service Coverage Ratio): Financial metric assessing debt servicing capability.
- DSCR_DATE: The date when the DSCR was last calculated.
- APPRAISAL_DATE: The date of the most recent property appraisal.
- ENDING_SCHEDULE_BALANCE: The scheduled balance of the loan at the end of the period.
- LOAN_ID: Unique identifier for each individual loan.
- MATURITY_DATE: The date when the loan is due to be paid off.
- NET_OPERATING_INCOME: Revenue remaining after operating expenses are deducted.
- PROPERTY_TYPE: Category defining the type of property securing the loan.
- PROS_ID: Unique identifier for each Property Reporting Obligation Status.
- REMAINING_AMORT_TERM: The remaining period for loan amortization.
- RESOLUTION_STRATEGY_CODE: Code signifying the approach taken to resolve loan issues.
- SERVICING_TRANSFER_DATE: The date when loan servicing was transferred.
- SPECIAL_SERVICING_COMMENTS: Comments related to specific loan servicing actions.
- STATE: The U.S. state where the property securing the loan is located.

This dataset is a paid dataset however the data itself is freely available on the edgar sec.gov site and many other sites: https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/0001780131/000188852423010151/bub19c04_ex991-202307.htm. The cost associated with this dataset is for the data pipelines to extract this data from Edgar system on a daily basis, simple quality checks and basic transformations, and loading this data into Snowflake data warehouse.

Data Wrangling for this dataset was performed by Aanya Kongettira
Data Scraping\Pipelining for this dataset was performed by Drew Bittenbender

description:
ESG metrics for 44 impact KPIs for 50 leading companies ESG metrics for up to 44 impact KPIs for 50 leading companies, with flags for whether the data is from company disclosures or GIST Impact models. This listing provides a sample comprising data pertaining to 50 leading companies. The GIST universe dataset contains over 13,000 listed entities.

Description

Raw data is crawled from publicly available company disclosures using our cognitive search engine. The data undergoes validation by our team of expert analysts to identify, verify and document outliers. Following reprocessing and data appending, the data undergoes algorithmic assurance before final approval by team leads specialising in each area of impact. The combination of human and machine quality control delivers a high level of confidence in the accuracy of the data.

Disclosure is incomplete even for GHG emissions, which is the most standardised non-financial disclosure. The lack of data is significantly higher in emerging markets compared with developed and certain sectors particularly lacking disclosure. Water usage and waste generation data are much sparser than GHG emissions.

Benchmark-based models are commonly used in the industry. The benchmarking approach uses the average emissions of the companies belonging to a particular business activity to predict the emissions of companies with no disclosures, by extrapolating the emissions based on revenues. Estimations are linearly proportional to the revenue generated by the company. This approach ignores that most large business have revenues from multiple sectors and that location is particularly important when assessing impact. Statistically, each estimated value has the same standard deviation, which leads to very limited co-relation between estimated and actual values.

GIST Impact’s machine learning approach to modelled data takes into consideration unique financial and non-financial data points for each company. A unique list of companies is identified to create the nearest neighbour group and then an average value is generated for extrapolation. Six different unique operational parameters are taken into consideration to identify the peer group.

The model accounts for multiple business activities and the peer group accurately captures the variability from operations, location, and performance, thereby reducing the deviation between actual emissions and estimates.

Description
SDG alignment is a means of holding companies accountable and setting and monitoring goals for investment portfolios. The UN SDGs are the most widely recognised and accepted non-regulatory standards and form best practice in sustainability target setting at corporate and investment level.

GIST Impact valuations use the Drivers-Outcomes-Impacts approach, whereby the change in economic conditions caused by an ESG metric, such as air pollution, are sourced from global databases and valued using peer-reviewed scientific and economic research. Results are typically negative for environmental impacts and positive for social and financial value added.

These monetary values are then mapped to the UN SDGs at the target level. This allows both positive and negative values to align with individual goals and exposure may be assessed at both gross and net levels.

The GIST Impact methodology is aligned with the most widely adopted impact frameworks from organisations such as the United Nations, the Capitals Coalition, Impact Weighted Accounts Initiative, and the Value Balancing Alliance. The methodology aligns with ISSB.

title: Sustainability Raw Data Disclosed & Modelled
description:
ESG metrics for 44 impact KPIs for 50 leading companies ESG metrics for up to 44 impact KPIs for 50 leading companies, with flags for whether the data is from company disclosures or GIST Impact models. The full data set is available for over 13,000 companies worldwide.

Description

Raw data is crawled from publicly available company disclosures using our cognitive search engine. The data undergoes validation by our team of expert analysts to identify, verify and document outliers. Following reprocessing and data appending, the data undergoes algorithmic assurance before final approval by team leads specialising in each area of impact. The combination of human and machine quality control delivers a high level of confidence in the accuracy of the data.

Disclosure is incomplete even for GHG emissions, which is the most standardised non-financial disclosure. The lack of data is significantly higher in emerging markets compared with developed and certain sectors particularly lacking disclosure. Water usage and waste generation data are much sparser than GHG emissions.

Benchmark-based models are commonly used in the industry. The benchmarking approach uses the average emissions of the companies belonging to a particular business activity to predict the emissions of companies with no disclosures, by extrapolating the emissions based on revenues. Estimations are linearly proportional to the revenue generated by the company. This approach ignores that most large business have revenues from multiple sectors and that location is particularly important when assessing impact. Statistically, each estimated value has the same standard deviation, which leads to very limited co-relation between estimated and actual values.

GIST Impact’s machine learning approach to modelled data takes into consideration unique financial and non-financial data points for each company. A unique list of companies is identified to create the nearest neighbour group and then an average value is generated for extrapolation. Six different unique operational parameters are taken into consideration to identify the peer group.

The model accounts for multiple business activities and the peer group accurately captures the variability from operations, location, and performance, thereby reducing the deviation between actual emissions and estimates.

title: Biodiversity Data - Sample
description:
GIST Impact’s Biodiversity impact data for 8 KPIs together with sectoral benchmarks for 14,000+ companies. GIST Impact’s Biodiversity dataset calculates the potential “species extinction risk” posed by a company’s direct operations on nature and biodiversity. The outputs include impacts on terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. 
GIST Impact uses the latest LCIA method (based on the drivers-outcomes-impacts pathway) to calculate the biodiversity footprint of a company as a result of 8 direct and indirect drivers: GHG emissions, Air Pollution (NOx and SOx), Water consumption, Water & land pollution (Total Nitrogen and Total Phosphorous), Land use change and Waste generation. Salient features of GIST Impact’s biodiversity data:
1.	Based on actual data: The impacts are calculated from actual company disclosed data and can be traced back to the source. In absence of disclosed data, estimated data from GIST Impact’s Machine Learning models are used.
2.	 Geographic apportionment: The impacts are geographically apported based on the company’s operational locations. 
3.	Output metric: The metric for the biodiversity dataset is the global Potentially Disappeared Fraction (PDF) of species, also referred to as “extinction risk”. To help visualize the scope of impacts, GIST Impact also provides the outputs in tCO2e equivalent numbers of PDF. 
4.	Impacts from waste generation: While waste generation contributes significantly to impacts on nature and biodiversity, most LCIA methods do not provide the Characterization Factors (CFs) for its waste. GIST Impact has calculated the CFs for waste generation based on other drivers and includes it in the dataset.

title: Cost Optimizer for Snowflake
description:
Understanding your credit leakages  Introduction
There are several risk factors involved with determining cost optimization in Snowflake, and as a result, clients may have concerns about whether those risks are worth the reward. The common concerns we hear include the high initial cost and the necessary experimentation with Snowflake’s platform for performance and recommendations on design decisions.

Here are a few of the most frequently asked questions that our team receives from new, Snowflake clients in their first-year journey:

"We followed the best practices recommended by Snowflake in multiple webinars, blogs, and documentation. They do work well, but they come with a huge credit cost. 
-	What really went wrong?
-	How can optimal performance be achieved at a justified cost?
-	What clustering keys should be used?
-	What’s the right size of the warehouse to be used?"

There are strong query performance optimization methods available in Snowflake including materialized view, clustering, and search optimization. Each optimization method is designed for different scenarios, and if it is used in the wrong scenario, this can lead to an unexpected result. Additionally, selecting the wrong choice of optimization method can lead to higher costs.

NTT DATA understands these questions and concerns, and as a result, we were motivated to build our “Cost Optimizer for Snowflake”.

The "Cost Optimizer for Snowflake" App Analyses, scrutinizes and optimizes following Snowflake cost areas across the platform: 
- Managed compute warehouse cost 
- Storage cost
- Server less compute including:
	- Auto-clustering
	- Materialized Views
	- Pipes

Following sections briefly describes each section in the app.

Overview 
The overview section highlights summary of credit usage at organization level as well as at account level which includes:
-	Weekly cost in various snowflake accounts within the organization and how it is different from previous week
-	Segregation of cost by service types at organization and account level
-	Most frequent users and Databases used
-	Top costly queries and their cost and frequency 

This section is helpful to prioritize the cost optimization efforts.

Warehouse Utilization
The warehouse utilization section takes deep dive into the warehouse utilization. This includes:
-	Unutilized but billed warehouse time and possible saving
-	Bytes spilled to local/remote disks and possibility of upscaling warehouses
-	Utilization of data cache
-	Queue load on warehouses and possibility of use of multi-cluster warehouses

Auto Clustering
This section investigates the clustered tables and tables which possibly benefit from clustering along with the recommendation on clustering key. This section inspects the query log to identify the best cluster key.  This section includes capabilities including:
-	Analysis on how frequently table is re-clustered and how frequently it is queried
-	Potential savings if auto-reclustering is removed from less frequently queried but frequently updated table
-	Analysis of if columns used in joins and where clause are other than cluster key
-	Recommendation on cluster key

Materialized Views
      This section investigates materialized views, their cost, frequency of use and frequency of refresh. This section also gives recommendations about following:
-	Potential saving if less frequently used but frequently refreshed materialized view are replaced by standard views/static tables
-	Potential candidate views for materialized view

Snowpipe
This section analyses the snowpipe usage to identify average file size, number of files etc. This section also recommends following:
-	File sizes
-	Potential savings

Storage
This section investigates storage uses and identifies unused storage in the account. This section also recommends following:
-	Candidate tables for drop
-	Potential saving on storage if table is dropped

Settings
This section provides flexibility to change the frequency of execution of cost optimizer in the background. All cost optimizers will be executed on the selected schedule to minimize the manual efforts.

title: Test Automation for Snowflake
description:
Automate the data quality monitoring About the “Test Automation for Snowflake”
We know that data accuracy and quality are crucial to making business decisions. During the ETL/ELT process, it’s necessary to keep an eye on data quality. Why? The manual efforts and time required for testing data quality can be very costly. While automation tools exist in the market, moving data from the Snowflake environment to conduct data quality testing has the potential to raise security concerns, especially when it comes to sensitive data.
As your Trusted Global Innovator, NTT DATA understands that data security is a priority for a variety of businesses and industries. To help us put your data first, we built a framework, known as “Test Automation for Snowflake” that conducts data testing without moving data out of the Snowflake environment and without the need for manual efforts.
"Test Automation for Snowflake" app provides the following capabilities: 
- Add data quality test cases and schedule them
- Data quality results with patterns
- Data ingestion error analysis
- Functional testing of UDF/Stored Procedures


Overview 
The overview section in the app visually represents number of data quality checks failed in last 30 days on various databases if any data quality checks are applied. This section also answers: How many checks are added per databases? When is the data last modified in various databases?  How many records are failed during data ingestion?  This section will be almost blank Just after the installation of the app but very useful after data quality checks are added and executed over the period. 

DQ Test Results
This section visualizations the data quality test results if any quality checks already executed. This section also facilitates to explore test results that are based on Test IDs or table names. The test results dashboard shows test results along with changes over the period. Sometimes it is useful to take a deeper dive by looking at the pattern of test results over a period and correlating it with events like deployments/ETL changes etc. 

DQ Test Cases
This section shows list of data quality checks already added on a specific table. This section gives ability to filter it down to a particular table on which data quality checks are already added. 
This section also facilitates adding new data quality checks on a specific table in the snowflake environment. This also facilitates adding multiple data quality checks on multiple columns in one go to save time. There are two types of data quality checks present i.e.
-	Parameterized 
-	Non- Parameterized

The non-parameterized tests are those tests which doesn’t requires additional information, e.g., if quality check is “Column values need to be unique”, then it does not need any additional information.  Following are non-parameterized tests that are currently supported, if you need some quality check that is not present here, please contact us and we are more than happy to add that check into the list:
-	Expect Column Values to Be Unique
-	Expect Column Values to Not Be Null
-	Expect Column Values to Be Null
-	Expect Column Values to Be Increasing
-	Expect Column Values to Be Decreasing
-	Expect Column Values to Be Dateutil Parseable
-	Expect Column Values to Be Json Parseable

Parameterized Test cases are those test cases that requires additional information e.g., when you expect column values to be in defined set of values, then you need to specify that set as well.  Following are parameterized tests that are currently supported, If you need some quality check that is not present here, please contact us and we are more than happy to add that check into the list:
-	Expect Column Values to Be in Set
-	Expect Column Values to Be Between
-	Expect Column Values to Not Match Regex
-	Expect Column Values to Match Regex
If multiple parameters are required for the test, then add them as a comma separated list e.g. 
In case you expect Column values to be between 0 to 10000, then parameter should be:
0,10000

Execute Test
Test cases are supposed to be executed automatically on the predefined schedule but even you can execute them manually by entering the test case id if you need to.

Functional Test
Important business logic is incorporated into UDF and stored procedures in Snowflake. Here is the capability to unit test such functions. Select the function and enter your test input and expected output. click on test and functional test results will be displayed on the screen. 


Data Ingestion Quality
The app provides the capability to monitor Data ingestion quality in terms of number of errors reported/rows failed to load over the period.

Data Freshness
The app provides the capability to monitor the freshness of the data present in various tables in terms of last modified/refreshed. You can drill down through the filters to check freshness across the snowflake environment.

Settings
This section provides flexibility to change the frequency of execution of data quality checks. All data quality checks will be executed on the selected schedule to minimize the manual efforts.

description:
Petrochemical/NGL 
Since 1984, ESAI has been helping industry leaders and governments navigate critical transitions in the liquids energy markets. Trained in quantitative analysis, economics, political science, finance, and industrial policy—our team tracks supply, demand, price, regulation, and policy to provide timely insight on developments impacting the legacy and emerging energy markets.

ESAI Energy analyzes the petrochemical industry using a holistic approach that encompasses our expertise in the upstream oil market, geopolitical trends, petrochemical projects, industry and climate policies, as well as global and regional macroeconomics. Our comprehensive strategy allows us to leverage our vast database in combination with our forecasting expertise, providing clear insights to past, present and future interactions between feedstocks in response to market trends.

The dataset includes global and regional data for prices, supply, and demand for each feedstock, with selected country level data for supply, demand, inventories, and trade. Moreover, we collect and estimate monthly and annual production data on primary petrochemicals, such as ethylene and propylene, with data added on a consistently, ongoing basis.

Based on our proprietary petrochemical dataset, we also present historical and future capacity by region and selected countries for ethylene and PDH. We break down ethylene capacity by regional/country and by feedstocks and update the capacity datasets by diligent tracking of global project & development information.

ESAI Energy additionally follows developments beyond the petrochemical industry for LPG and naphtha. This includes consumption in the residential, commercial, and transportation sectors, in consideration of consumer behavior and seasonal patterns. These factors affect pricing and petrochemical production margins.

This data is based on the Infracommunal Reference System (IRIS), which is a statistical geographic unit utilized by the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) to analyze and publish demographic and socio-economic data. IRIS are subdivisions of communes, which are the smallest administrative division in France. IRIS have a population size ranging from 1,800 to 5,000 inhabitants, and their boundaries are determined by the distribution of residential buildings. IRIS are used to provide a fine-grained geographical level for the analysis and dissemination of statistical data related to population, housing, employment, and other social and economic factors.

title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory in France
description:
(GES BILAN) This dataset contains public data on greenhouse gas emissions from various organizations, gathered from the ADEME platform. The information provided varies depending on the organization type, but includes the emissions report ID, organization name, reporting year, employee/population count, and activity description. Additionally, data on emissions reductions, action plans, and sustainable development policies are available for certain organization types. Methodology information is also provided. For full methodology details, refer to the online publication.


Here is a list of the variables present in the Bilan GES data, with comments from the metadata:

ID du Bilan GES: This identifier allows the Bilan GES to be quickly located via its link: https://www.bilans-ges.ademe.fr/fr/bilanenligne/detail/index/idElement/ID/back/bilans.

Type de structure: This refers to the type of structure to which the Bilan GES relates.

Type de collectivité: This variable only concerns Bilans GES of collectivities.

Raison sociale / Nom de l'entité: This is the legal name or entity name for which the Bilan GES was produced.

Année de reporting: This variable indicates the year to which the Bilan GES relates. By default, it is displayed as of January 1st of the specified year.

Date de publication: This is the date on which the Bilan GES was published.

Nombre de salariés / d'agents: This variable indicates the number of employees or agents for the entity concerned by the Bilan GES.

Population: This variable only concerns Bilans GES of collectivities.

Mode de consolidation: This refers to the consolidation mode used for the Bilan GES.

Descriptif sommaire de l’activité: This variable does not exist for Bilans GES of collectivities.

SIREN: This variable indicates the SIREN for the consolidated BEGES of several SIREN. Only the head office SIREN is displayed here.

APE(NAF): This variable only concerns Bilans GES of Businesses, Associations and Public Institutions.

Libellé: This is the label corresponding to APE(NAF) for Bilans GES of Businesses, Associations and Public Institutions.

Région: This variable indicates the region to which the entity for which the Bilan GES was produced belongs.

Ville: This variable indicates the city to which the entity for which the Bilan GES was produced belongs.

Une année de référence a été calculée: This variable indicates if a reference year has been calculated for the Bilan GES.

Emission publication P1 to P23 : carbon emissions published by the entity

title: Inter-Regime Health Insurance Expenses in France (DAMIR)
description:
DAMIR (Dépenses d'Assurance maladie Inter Régimes) database This dataset is an extraction from the National Inter-Regime Health Insurance System (SNIIRAM) covering all health insurance reimbursements across all regimes in France between 2009 and 2021. 

In order to preserve the anonymity of healthcare professionals and patients, the geographical axes are limited:
- to 9 geographical zones (study and territorial planning zones) which are groupings of administrative regions from 2009 to 2014, refered to as ZEAT (Zone d'Emploi à Agglomération de Taille intermédiaire) which means the Intermediate-sized Agglomeration Employment Zone.
- to 13 geographical zones (close to the newly created large administrative regions) from 2015 onwards, refered to as REG for Region.

Expenses are detailed according to six analytical axes (period, service, payer organization, care beneficiary, performing healthcare professional, prescribing healthcare professional) and seven amount (total expense, reimbursement basis, amount reimbursed, excess) and volume (number, quantity, coefficient) indicators. In total, each service line is described by 55 variables. It is essential to refer to the dataset description accompanying the data.

title: Global Historical Lightning Data - Sample
description:
Worldwide gridded lightning data for risk assessment, reporting, and analysis. Analyzing historic lightning events helps you better understand and mitigate the risks to your people, property, and operations. Businesses use lightning data to improve the planning and management of safety-critical operations while reducing costly downtime. 

Vaisala Xweather lightning data meets the needs of the energy, defense, maritime, construction, and insurance industries with best-in-class lightning data from its fully owned and operated global lightning detection networks.

This sample data set includes gridded historical lightning data for 1 year (2019) for an area of approximately 745,000 km2 covering parts of Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mexico, and the Gulf of Mexico, and major cities such as Austin, Dallas, and Houston.

The complete dataset includes five years (2017-2021) of gridded lightning data for the entire globe including land and sea. Vaisala Xweather provides lighting data for any location, region, or geography. If you would like to purchase data, please contact us using the Contact Vaisala link in the listing.

Sample/Tables included:
LIGHTNING DENSITY SAMPLE

Fields included:
- YEAR
- LAT — latitude, defining the center of each 0.2° grid area
- LONG — longitude, defining the center of each 0.2° grid area  
- DENSITY — the number of lightning events per square km per year

Suggested uses for business intelligence:
- Energy: evaluating locations for wind farms and solar power plants
- Land management: risk assessment for forest fires  
- Defense: planning training operations 
- Maritime: risk analysis and route planning 
- Insurance: risk analysis, and claim assessments 
- Meteorological agencies:  thunderstorm and lightning climatology research  

Data format and granularity: 
Gridded lightning density data (lightning events per square km, per year), suitable for map display, analysis, research, and risk assessment. Each grid is 0.2 degrees of latitude by 0.2 degrees of longitude, which is about 22 km by 22 km at the equator, getting progressively smaller as you move toward the poles. 

Each grid has a single lightning density value of events per square kilometer per year. Lightning events include cloud-to-ground strokes and in-cloud pulses, together called 'total lightning.' 

The sample dataset includes gridded historical lightning data for 1 year (2019) for a region from 34° N, 102° W to 27° N, 92° W.

Sources
The dataset comes from the Global Lightning Detection Network (GLD360) and the U.S. National Lighting Detection Network (NLDN). These proprietary networks are owned and operated by Vaisala. Together, these networks detect more than 2 billion lightning events every year.

NLDN is the longest continuously operating and most scientifically validated lightning detection network in the world. NLDN has been the primary source of lightning information for major organizations including the National Weather Service, Federal Aviation Administration, and the United States Air Force for more than 30 years. The largest electric power utilities in the United States use NLDN to help manage the reliability of their transmission and wind power assets.

Vaisala’s GLD360 is the only truly global lightning detection network and has been detecting lightning worldwide since 2009. GLD360 is the most advanced and accurate long-range lightning detection network in the world, instantly detecting lightning anywhere over land and sea. GLD360 is trusted by global organizations including the National Weather Service, the United States Navy, and the Deutscher Wetterdienst to provide real-time data for the accurate detection of lightning anywhere on the planet.

title: US TTB COLA Registry Alcohol Product Catalog - Demo
description:
Demo edition of the full US TTB COLA Registry, limited to 2018. In the US, alcohol product labels must undergo a regulatory approval process facilitated by the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB).

Alcohol producers digitally submit their prospective labels along with supporting documents to the TTB, and these application materials are published to the TTB's Public COLA Registry (COLA refers to a Certificate of Label Approval). 

This registry contains over 2MM application records dating back to the late 90's, and the registry adds ~3K new records each week. In addition to the label imagery,
these applications include a form with ~20 structured fields describe the product and the manufacturer.

These records are great representation of alcohol products soon-to-be available in retail locations in the US market.

COLA Cloud scrapes, parses and enriches the TTB's Public COLA Registry. In addition to all the structured fields of each COLA, the COLA Cloud pipeline includes OCR via the best-in-class Google Cloud Vision API on every label image (a $6,000 value over 4M images) to provide label text as a column, and. reads barcodes from label images (~25% of applications contain a unique barcode).

The demo edition of this dataset includes the entire year of 2018. The `colas` table contains ~170K rows. All the features of COLA Cloud are included.

• Search Term - Human readable identifier

description:

description:
Standardize and enrich disparate clinical data  IMO’s deep expertise in clinical data is grounded in terminology used by over 740,000 US physicians during point-of-care documentation. IMO Precision Normalize leverages this foundation to efficiently standardize inconsistent clinical data from diverse systems into consistent, structured, clinically validated terminology that is comprehensively mapped to standard code systems behind the scenes.  IMO Precision Normalize helps organizations across the health IT ecosystem to enrich clinical data, accelerate data readiness for analytics, and power accurate insights. 

Features 

1. Industry-leading clinical terminology: Every IMO solution starts with a foundation of the definitive source of clinical terminology, managing the complexity of 5.0 million clinical terms with current and comprehensive mappings to all major global coding systems:
-- Problem/Diagnosis: ICD-9-CM, ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT® 
-- Procedure: CPT®, ICD-10-PCS, HCPCS, LOINC, SNOMED CT® 
-- Medication: RxNorm, NDC 

2. Robust normalization engine: The engine that drives IMO Precision Normalize is capable of processing up to 300,000 terms per minute across diagnosis, procedure, medication, and laboratory data domains.  By comparing input data to IMO’s clinically-vetted, highly specific, and propriety terminology, the engine accurately matches most terms with a high degree of confidence to minimize manual review.   

3. Description and code-based matching: Client supplied clinical descriptions or codes pertaining to problems, diagnoses, procedures and labs, and medications are matched to IMO terms. The engine’s matching algorithms can account for both exact and fuzzy matches of descriptions. 

4. API or Bulk endpoint deployment: IMO’s solution can be deployed in several ways, including a one-time run to clean up a legacy data mart, or via a near real-time API interaction to ensure that data is immediately correct throughout an organization’s systems.   

5. Auto domain resolution: In cases where the domain (problem, procedure, or medication) of a description is unknown, the engine can attempt to automatically detect a term’s domain and match it appropriately.  

6. Data review tools: Map manager UI enables simple and flexible review of matches by domain, volume of use, and confidence score.  Enables accelerated localization, remapping, and follow-up normalization operations. 

Improve clinical data quality – at scale 

1. Enrich clinical data: Built on a dictionary of 5 million terms and comprehensive mapping to all appropriate standard code systems behind the scenes 

2. Accelerate data review: Increase the accuracy of normalized data with an intuitive interface to review, accept, and adjust matched data as needed 

3. Reduce maintenance burden: IMO content is updated 6 times a year to be compliant with health system and regulatory requirements 

4. Increase data specificity: Foundational terminology is curated by clinical SMEs, increasing the accuracy and specificity of terms and codes

Expected workflow:
-- Request access to this listing and an IMO representative will reach out 
-- Work with the IMO team to create an account and agreement 
-- Once the agreement is finalized, configure the Snowflake connector
-- Use Snowpipe to extract from internal or external stage and write to Snowflake staging table
-- Create a function or task to extract from staging table and write to Target table

title: Equity Options Close Mark
description:
Analyzing Market Trends and Volatility Patterns in Equity Options Data Description:
SpiderRock’s Option Closing Marks is a unique set of over 50 data fields including the SR closing mark and an exchange closing mark. Data featured includes the closing quotes, closing prices, SpiderRock’s closing underlier bid, following with option bid, ask and mark (Closing time minus 1 minute), option implied bid/ask volatilities, Greeks, dividend data, surface volatilities and prices, and calculations on both the option and its underlier. Prior day closing quotes and prices are also included. Typical Use Cases:
Some typical uses for this data include back-testing, incubating/optimizing strategies, trade-cost analysis (TCA), model market volatility and relative market movement, replay market patterns, and accurate compliance reporting. Additional Information: 1. Data Quality
Closing mark records are bases for the volatility surface PnL calculations in the SpiderRock platform ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and corrections if needed. SpiderRock’s proprietary approach selects the most appropriate closing price for the given security type and surface prices. This process significantly reduces the effort required to reconcile bad closing marks and provide consistent day-to-day results that reduce frustrating mark noise and better represent a Sharpe Ratio. 2. Data Presentation
Data is collected point-in-time and archived from our trading platform's ticker plant. The format of the data is consistent with our real-time volatility feed and live analytics. The dataset is organized in multiple columns with each column representing a different data point. 3. Data Sources
Our historical data is derived from the live data and analytics which powers the SpiderRock trading system and ensures a high level of accuracy and consistency. The data is also properly labeled, point in time and duplicates have been removed and basic data cleaning has been performed to improve the quality of the information. SpiderRock evaluates the data for validity and accuracy and performs statistical checks on the production databases daily to verify completeness.

title: Life Segment Fixed-Point Survey
provider: 株式会社エイトハンドレッド (Eight Hundred, Inc.)
description:
Consumer Trends,Lifestyle 
The Life Segment Fixed-Point Survey publishes time-series data on 16 items related to consumer trends and lifestyles, surveyed quarterly from 10,000 people nationwide.

In times of significant changes in consumer values and behaviors, accurate exploration of customer needs and continuous tracking of consumer trends become crucial for developing new businesses, services, and products. We have developed a platform where anyone can freely analyze and download this consumer data for use as macro-trend data supporting strategic initiatives or as foundational data for the latest consumer insights.

We aim to contribute to companies and society at large by making parts of our consumer research public.

Survey Overview:
- Method: Internet survey
- Target: 10,400 men and women aged 20-69 nationwide (Macromill monitor members)
- Allocation Method: Based on 2015 National Census demographics (area, gender, age group)
- Timing: Annually in January, April, July, October (four times a year, end of each month)
- Commissioned by: Macromill, Inc.

Supplementary Information:
- Cross-tabulation axes definitions:

- Generations:
  - Baby Boomers: Born 1953-1963
  - Generation X: Born 1964-1980
  - Generation Y: Born 1981-1994
  - Generation Z: Born 1995-2010

- Life Stages:
  - Single: Divorced, widowed, or never married
  - Married without children: Living only with a spouse
  - Youngest child preschool-aged: Living with a preschool-aged child
  - Youngest child in elementary school: Living with an elementary school-aged child
  - Youngest child in middle/high school: Living with a middle or high school student
  - Youngest child in college or older: Living with a child in college or higher education
  - Seniors (65 and older): Regardless of marital status or children

- Life Fulfillment:
  - Fulfilled: Respondents who feel close to 'feeling fulfilled in life'
  - Unfulfilled: Respondents who feel close to 'lacking a sense of fulfillment in life'

Dataset fields include:
- survey_time: Date of survey
- question1: Main category of question
- question2: Subcategory of question
- question3: Specific question item
- question_type: Type of question (e.g., SA, MA, N)
- answer_code: Code for response option
- answer_label: Label for response option
- target1: Main respondent group
- target2: Subdivision within respondent group
- rate_of_answer: Response score

Use Cases:
- Market Trend Analysis: Identify and track emerging trends in consumer behavior and preferences.
- Targeted Marketing: Use demographic data to refine marketing strategies and campaigns.
- Product Development: Leverage insights into consumer needs for designing new products or enhancing existing ones.
- Academic Research: Provide a rich data source for studies in sociology, economics, and marketing.
- Public Policy: Aid in developing policies and programs that align with current consumer sentiments and needs.

Regarding the Use of Data:
- Copyright: Owned by Eight Hundred Inc. When quoting or reproducing, please always credit 'Researched by Eight Hundred Inc.'
- Modification and reproduction of part or all of the survey data is prohibited. The survey data may be changed, modified, or deleted without notice.

Data Sales:
- We do not generally sell the survey data.
- However, downloading and secondary use of data from the published dashboard are allowed.

自社データにオープンデータを掛け合わせることで、データ分析の高度化を実現できます。

CO-ODE is a service that processes and distributes open data published by national and local governments in an easy-to-use manner.
By using CO-ODE, the workload of collecting, processing, and updating various open data is eliminated.
Anyone can easily acquire the data and use it for factor analysis, cause analysis, and future prediction.
By combining open data with your own data, you can achieve advanced data analysis.

Separating company emissions into these scopes increases the transparency and comparability of corporate emissions reporting.

description:
2022 Northern Trains station demographic data. **Introduction and Scope:** This dataset provides an overview of the demographics and public transport options surrounding train stations managed exclusively by Northern Trains in the United Kingdom. It is designed as an enhancement tool that allows users to correlate station-specific data with the socio-economic and transportation characteristics of the areas immediately surrounding each station. Each entry is linked to a specific station using the CRS code, ensuring that users can easily integrate this data with other railway or geographic information systems.


**Data Points Included:** Public Transport Options: Detailed listings of available public transport services other than trains (e.g., bus lines, tram links, cycling paths) accessible within a half-mile radius of the stations. Parking Options: Details of free and paid car and bicycle parking spaces Staffing Levels: How many staff are on hand at the station to service customer needs. Political Affiliation: Who the MP is for the region the station exists within as well as their political party. Footfall: ORR footfall for the stations between 2019 - 2020 and 2020 – 2021 Rail Service Levels: The number of services which stop at the station per day


**Value to Consumers:** This dataset is invaluable for:


Transportation Planning: Helping transportation authorities and local governments assess the adequacy of current transport services and plan for future infrastructure needs based on detailed demographic insights. Urban Development: Assisting urban developers and planners in understanding the demographic landscape of areas surrounding the stations for targeted residential or commercial projects. Market Analysis: Enabling businesses and service providers to tailor products and services to the demographics of specific areas, optimizing outreach and market penetration strategies. Academic Research: Providing researchers with rich, geospatially-encoded data crucial for studies on urban mobility, socioeconomic factors, and their impacts on public transportation usage.

title: Threat Intelligence Database
description:
Get the latest cyber threats, including malware, phishing, C2 (C&C), botnets, and other malicious activity. THIS SHARE IS LIMITED TO A WEEK'S WORTH OF DATA FROM THE PREVIOUS MONTH

Our daily Threat Intelligence Database gives you actionable insights into the latest cyber threats, including malware, phishing, C2 (C&C), botnets, and other malicious activity. Choose from raw or pre-filtered data feeds that seamlessly integrate with your security systems, allowing you to detect and respond to threats and safeguard your business quickly.

Review our website to access the complete Threat Intelligence Database (https://falconsentinel.com/threat-database/?ref=sf).

Formats included:
- Malicious IPv4/IPv6 address data feeds
- Malicious domain name data feed
- Malicious URL data feed
- Malicious CIDR data feed

Fields included:
- ip – IoC: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. IPv6 feed also contains IPv4 addresses represented in the IPv6 notation.
- cidr – IoC: IPv4 and IPv6 ranges in CIDR notation. IPv6 feed also contains IPv4 ranges represented in the IPv6 notation.
- domainName – IoC: domain name.
- url – IoC: URL. It might be absolute (https://example.com/files/badfile.php) or relative (/files/badfile.php). Relative URLs do not have a corresponding domainName field.
- host – Domain name or IP for absolute URLs.
- threatType – The threat type associated with the IoC. One of the following: attack, botnet, c2, malware, phishing, spam, suspicious, tor, generic.
- lastSeen – UNIX timestamp when the activity was detected last time.

The complete database (https://falconsentinel.com/threat-database/documentation?ref=sf) covers the following 9 threat types:
- Attack: malicious activity detected from the host. For example, SSH brute-force, etc.
- Botnet: a host was detected as an actor in a group of connected hosts that perform malicious activities (botnet).
- C2 or C&C: the host is a known botnet's "Command and Control" server.
- Malware: the IoC is related to malicious software distribution. It can be a host or a URL serving the malware.
- Phishing: the indicator, usually a domain name or URL, is involved in Phishing activity.
- Spam: a host engaged in sending spam.
- Suspicious: IoC's activity hasn't been verified to be of malicious nature. For instance, it may be a host scraping websites, sending large amounts of ICMP queries, etc.
- Tor: a host acts as a TOR exit node.
- Generic: IoC has been involved in some form of malicious activity but couldn't be classified into one of the other categories.

Our Threat Intelligence Database is powered by multiple sources, ensuring you receive comprehensive and accurate information to protect your organization. Our sources include the following:
- Server logs: we scrutinize server logs to detect unusual activity and unauthorized access attempts.
- Honeypots: we use decoy systems called honeypots to attract attackers and gather intelligence on the latest attack methods.
- OSINT: we collect threat intelligence from open sources such as social media, forums, and blogs to stay informed on emerging threats and trends.
- Abuse reports (ISPs): we monitor abuse reports from internet service providers to identify potential threats and malicious activity.
- Our own researches: our team of experts conducts in-depth research to identify new and emerging threats and provide a comprehensive analysis of existing threats.

Introducing the Food Safety Notifications dataset, including notifications from the EU Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF). When a member state detects a health hazard, it promptly notifies the entire network about the affected product and the actions taken to mitigate the risk. These actions may involve withholding, recalling, seizing, or rejecting the products in question.

Included countries in the dataset are all EU member states and EEA countries (Norway, Liechtenstein and Iceland).

Including fields like notification ID, validation date, reference number, notifying country, notification subject, product category, product type, notification classification, risk decision, and publication status, this dataset offers valuable insights into food safety issues. title: Semantic Layer (Enterprise Edition)
meta_info: 360-Degree Customer View,Customer Onboarding,Regulatory Reporting,Machine Learning,Performance & Cost
description:
Honeydew Semantic Layer is a shared source of truth for business logic on Snowflake Note: Honeydew offers various tiers of the product. This is the Enterprise Edition listing. For the differences between the editions see https://honeydew.ai/pricing

Honeydew is a Semantic Layer built on top of Snowflake.
Honeydew makes sure that any business metric, such as MRR, Churn, or Daily Active Users, can be defined once and calculated the same way for every consumer.

How does it work:

1) Customer onboards with Honeydew and sets up their account.

2) Customer imports their existing semantics into Honeydew. These can come from a BI tool (e.g. Tableau workbooks, or LookML models), from the ETL (e.g. dbt models, SQL queries or stored procedures code), or just be newly created on top of existing tables in Snowflake.

3) The semantics can be consumed in a number of ways:

- A JDBC proxy, that can support any BI tool, send queries to the Honeydew Semantic Layer. Honeydew will translate these queries to the actual Snowflake queries. Snowflake will execute these queries and the results will be provided back to the BI tool.

- Creating dynamic datasets based on the semantics. Each dataset can be then deployed to Snowflake, as a view or a table, or exported as a a dbt model.

- Querying the semantics directly from within Snowflake, using the table functions and procedures provided with the Honeydew Native App.

title: Ava-Watch Real Time Query Monitor
description:
Monitor long running queries and send alerts when exceeding set threshold. This app is to prevent runaway queries consuming unexpected credits in your system. Once you set up the app first time, you will receive an alert if there are queries running longer than the threshold you defined. You can then decide which actions to take, either leave the query running or kill the query if it is indeed problematic one.

Most users prefer to receive alerts in email.  Currently, snowflake Native App does not support email.   Follow instructions from readme file to set up email outside Native App,  those steps are simple and straightforward.

Warehouse credit will be consumed when the App start monitoring your snowflake just like when running any queries. The amount of credits consumed depends on how frequent you like the monitor to run.
